messages.s_71e561b6b9d75690515f30ae93ff72fc091059: Karate A: kihon alignment and original sequence preparation
messages.s_5ee47907e8556acb9f8001b0ad4bdbc050f5e8: Shotokan-oriented beginner preparation. Short positions and paused movements are explicit preparation adaptations here; they are not presented as standard technique for every school.
messages.s_943acf4d333bbbb83a3a22dfd82182685a7683: Review draft for an adult beginner. It is not a children’s program, rehabilitation or an individual suitability decision. Previous boxing/kickboxing study does not replace karate prerequisites.
messages.s_619c5b409301a6338c3f52aab507485c45e5a0: KA-P1 is an original JabLab practice sequence; it is not Heian Shodan, Taikyoku Shodan or an accepted shortened version of either. Named traditional kata, full karate curriculum, belt/rank, contact, kumite, impact power and self-defense competence are outside this result. Those parts of the broader goal remain open.
messages.s_767bfd5c0f5a5873b1cabb17d4b4de1d2e5b07: Stop movement for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, instability, knee/foot binding or uncertainty about safe movement. Do not try to overcome it with a sudden correction, extra depth or faster repetition. Return to a safe neutral position only if that is comfortable; tell the appropriate person about the help/adaptation needed. Do not plan a physical retest while symptoms remain. This text provides neither diagnosis nor health clearance.
messages.s_60ae1eb3f188706aace1df9a93bc8128eda18b: Right/left refer to the learner’s own body; do not assume a mirrored demonstration. N is a paper label for initial forward, and E its right quarter-turn direction; these are not geographic measurements. “Same side” means the hand on the side of the forward foot. A–D label the areas where the body settles; the feet are not stacked on one line.
messages.s_8c7f664627b97326567add6e17b071cde903ae: 1 · A · N · Parallel preparation, hands resting, complete pause.
messages.s_8df6f0d856df9361dd29e3159b77eb0df72ee1: 2 · B · N · Left foot small forward on its own track; settle left-forward and pause; both fists beside lower ribs → left gedan-barai/right hikite → pause → left returns by the short up-and-back path at its own side to left lower ribs, right hikite stays; pause with both in side preparation.
messages.s_de75525215a5ac3ef42dabbae0257389a235e4: 3 · C · N · Right rear foot passes forward on its own track; settle right-forward and pause; right short straight hand from right-side preparation, left hikite stays → pause → right returns along the same short path to right lower ribs; pause with both in side preparation.
messages.s_e56ce41e99c8196705e32b137ef314679df5f4: 4 · C · E · Rest hands; right front stays, left rear advances on its own track level with right; neutral pause → right-left-right-left walking N→E and pause → right foot small forward on its own track, settle right-forward and pause → both fists in side preparation → right gedan-barai/left hikite → pause → right returns up-and-back at its own side to right lower ribs, left hikite stays; pause.
messages.s_f4fbb29c6a576b664420131562ea55c6d6339d: 5 · D · E · Left rear foot passes forward on its own track; settle left-forward and pause → left short straight hand from left-side preparation, right hikite stays → pause → left returns along the same short path to left lower ribs; pause with both in side preparation.
messages.s_1a864e1076813c2aadb1c4e5ca1d6e99740bd7: 6 · D · E · Rest hands at sides; left front stays, right rear advances on its own right track level with left; settle both feet parallel and stop completely. Sequence finished. Separate exit: two right quarters at D E→S→W; right-left-right(to level) W to C; left quarter at C W→S; right-left-right(to level) S to A; two right quarters at A S→W→N, neutral pause. Every right quarter is right-left-right-left; the left is left-right-left-right; detailed footprints are in lessons 12/15. The exit is not a seventh unit.
messages.s_a38b1d1bf96932b8a761c9f3c4c12eac695331: Kihon studies basic movements; kata is a form/sequence transmitted within a particular school; kumite concerns partnered practice. This course prepares kihon alignment and sequence recall first. Memorizing an order alone establishes neither application nor defensive competence. A traditional form’s name, order and transitions must be verified within the chosen school; KA-P1 is an original exercise written here.
messages.s_327e4ebc61d1a8853d425471e05693ea2a7ad6: Explain the three terms in your own words. Create separate headings for KA-P1 and named traditional kata.

messages.s_91098825f2edcdee3a182f7135ca0f22e85cbd: No. KA-P1 is original preparation. Named-kata instruction and authorized rank examination are separate requirements; physical acceptance is also absent.

messages.s_bd74c91fb51e83265076d6effedb353aea80d4: Should the feet be on one line or the knees locked?
messages.s_709a84907ac12b4e7d8e47512244bfd7c4cdd7: No. Separate comfortable tracks and unlocked knees are preparation principles; suitable spacing and directions depend on individual review.
messages.s_ef9f7cd7ccde1cc9dac735a5187f2013fc2261: If you wrote a universal centimeter distance or angle, remove it and identify the personal position to review.

messages.s_9dcb9d837072c59c00782ad81b183f9043d03e: Start by considering an open hand. Curl the four fingers comfortably into the palm; the thumb is not trapped inside them and rests comfortably outside over the folded index/middle fingers. Maintain a straight comfortable wrist relationship between hand and forearm; do not seek position by bending the wrist up, down or sideways. Identify the index and middle base knuckles; strike no surface. Do not force a hand that cannot close comfortably.
messages.s_e0013f083ca8bd3ff999e7ccaa4f5342d73459: Mark the thumb outside and the wrist line on a hand sketch; turn an unknown detail into an instructor question.
messages.s_2e6c4b5ceedaec2dc8328f3fdb30e19fa88096: Does placing the thumb inside the fingers or steering the fist by bending the wrist fit this preparation?
messages.s_a77fdf5a58094a130a328a928b08bfd3733dcd: No. The thumb remains outside and the wrist in a comfortable straight relationship with the forearm. Choose drawing/writing when uncertain; do not verify by striking a target.
messages.s_0dfad57241db1b6f83598909cc2bcd5530c11f: If you confused wrist bending and forearm rotation, describe them separately; do not mark discomfort as corrected technique.
messages.s_e29fd55b1fbd970b0a94815aafef3e38fafd01: Hide the hand drawing and explain thumb, wrist and the contact boundary again.
messages.s_224a8dc6e893ef4e5f16a70ca78bf5ba8cebb4: Hikite here is the returning hand’s preparation position, not a partner-pulling application. In parallel preparation, one elbow bends comfortably near the torso and the fist comes beside the lower ribs with a comfortable palm-up orientation; do not squeeze the shoulder back or force the elbow behind. The other hand can occupy a small forward path with a soft elbow. Exchange roles slowly: one goes forward while the other returns beside the body. Keep the wrist unbent and the path short and comfortable.
messages.s_07fcd274da0e4a0946119bec5ccee559879778: Draw two arrows for the left hand’s role while the right goes forward, then reverse the roles.
messages.s_991a57d9b7cb2055bede9bd1177d5a4876f11d: Must the returning hand be pulled as far behind as possible?
messages.s_a0273917a91b6f0f779b9a195aa5722f8187ae: No. Retain comfortable preparation beside the lower ribs and a quiet shoulder; maximal pulling or partner application is not the goal.
messages.s_78edc89f242b22275b36d18daa231e07317751: If you described shoulder squeezing or wrist bending, separate the hand path and comfortable preparation position again.
messages.s_ca7257922340435b99520f5f5cb147b0e046c3: Hide the arrows and write the changing roles of both hands; record uncertainty if present.
messages.s_5503f395983cc675ab103e455558439f15fc66: Stationary preparation studies the hand path without adding a step. From the parallel start, move the chambered fist slowly into empty space on a middle-height path in front of the torso; the other hand comes quietly to hikite. The elbow points comfortably downward and remains soft near the end. Comfortable forearm rotation can bring the palm toward downward; retain the straight wrist relationship. Do not strike the elbow’s endpoint, raise the shoulder or swing the torso for speed. After a small pause, return comfortably along the same path to preparation.
messages.s_83c8c952054d21ed8d0b819c9ff3f926f2eb89: Write five short notes for hand, opposite hand, elbow, wrist and return.
messages.s_516195f4515c07d23d2a080294695c9983cb49: Does changing palm orientation require bending the wrist or locking the elbow?
messages.s_2c587e4697daa71e549145addaaa432fb28c95: No. Comfortable rotation is in the forearm; the wrist retains its straight relationship and the elbow its soft endpoint. The task does not prove impact ability.
messages.s_6690326de0855e86db35337fdbd58bc29887c5: If you described only the outward path, add the opposite hand’s position and quiet return.
messages.s_d7eb3c57ce94dd141d90ef56dd9e26f53df8ce: Hide the five notes and rewrite the order; a physical retest is considered only with the same P prerequisites retained.
messages.s_14f2d6f849c17154835e5190b3e86b2a666c54: A written answer is not technical observation. You can describe the hand path, but if you did not observe your wrist or knee position, say “I do not know.” Recovery, the other hand and comfortable breathing matter alongside the outward path. Increasing speed cannot conceal a problem. A seated open-hand trace may explain the preparation idea; it does not count as acceptance of standing karate technique.
messages.s_895031f4c68f44203e6c5c2ffb2bfcbe6e544f: Create three rows headed “recalled in writing / actually observed / not known.”
messages.s_4a831422bdeb8faa3b731868e6c2a5f306a047: You did not observe elbow position, but your answer matched the key. What do you record?
messages.s_0039aaaac39022fb9584402e77c5e5e290324b: I compared the written answer; the elbow and physical technique are unverified. An observed problem permits a concrete correction; an unobserved component retains an uncertainty record.
messages.s_94b063cafa69854cc91f00a0acf97ec15a4459: If you substituted assumed correctness for missing observation, replace it with “unobserved” and state the next feedback question.
messages.s_c330d11d86893d3bd0c5cb58d42a14290dffaf: Classify a second example in writing: “My other hand was not visible.” Do not turn uncertainty into a passing mark.
messages.s_f0d0afbe443490ee264555a88d93d8671e4426: Draw left-forward and right-forward footprint diagrams. In each, mark the front foot that stays, the rear foot advancing on its own track until level with it, the separate tracks and complete pause. Add the knee/foot relationship and space ahead for the exit.
messages.s_cddc041da032850909d72734b4658ca4c3745e: From left-forward, which foot moves in this proposal’s neutral exit, where does it stop, and what does a deep-stance source not prescribe for the individual?
messages.s_b51d7caf5aa31ad861f22fdfebda68d187bd14: The left front foot stays; the right rear foot advances on its own right track and stops level with the left without passing it. From right-forward, the right stays and the left rear foot advances on its own track until level with it. Feet remain separate/parallel at a comfortable width; then a complete pause. Depth, angle or load percentage is not an automatic prescription; personal suitability of this short exit also needs P3 review.
messages.s_95d6fda0b323c584d4e0ec564a95e79d0d4402: If your drawing pulls the front foot backward, passes the rear foot ahead or crosses the feet, rewrite the selected rear-foot-to-level exit. If the knee and foot are forced in different directions, record a stop/adaptation issue; a paper correction does not authorize physical practice.
messages.s_048341e7cd3be69e4b9335fb0cfca9742f694d: Hide both diagrams and write front foot stays → rear foot advances on its own track to level → both feet settle → stop for both sides.
messages.s_5207946daea4b18b48b3d0174f3e5e73852441: Pass the rear foot on its own track
messages.s_da924c8e5345dfa7eb7abf0866c5dcf2bd2529: From the short left-forward preparation, lift the right rear foot slowly and take it along its own right track into a comfortable right-forward position beyond the left foot. Do not drag it on the floor or cross it over the left foot; do not turn the knee while keeping the sole planted. First settle the feet, restore comfortable knee relationships and stop the torso; the hands add no technique. From a right-forward start, the left rear foot passes on its own left track. Return by exiting to neutral and making small ordinary walking steps while seeing the space, rather than a blind backward step.
messages.s_877938d47c89a43b5feceb0565d0fad3905205: Draw separate tracks for left-forward→right-forward and right-forward→left-forward. Mark the settling pause.
messages.s_69bcbf7dcd328265e65e32abaf20e3691db525: With the left foot forward, which foot passes forward and on which track?
messages.s_d924679c1cd0ce4422597133167e8f70ceae63: The right rear foot passes on its own right track, settling right-forward. From a right-forward start, the corresponding foot is the left; do not cross the feet.
messages.s_a0d28366695f24b9a27ee6b26abb4e94019dd7: If you confused this with a boxing follow-step, write that the rear foot passes forward here and identify the new forward side.
messages.s_ec697d78ab82eb9bdafa613ded545dd4313ee4: Without the diagram, write the outcome for both starts; do not fill the gap by imagining faster movement.
messages.s_d7b7c15ba87ce7ed80724c112d4426b5d1c03b: Oi-zuki preparation uses the hand on the side of the foot that comes forward. In this separated preparation, both fists start comfortably beside the lower ribs; elbows remain near the torso, shoulders quiet and palms comfortably toward upward. From left-forward, the right rear foot passes on its own track; settle completely and stop right-forward. Then the right fist travels from its right-side preparation on a short straight path; the left stays quietly in left hikite. After a pause, bend the right elbow comfortably and bring the right fist back along the same short path beside the right lower ribs; comfortable forearm rotation brings the palm toward upward while retaining the straight wrist relationship. From right-forward, the left foot passes; after settling, the left works and returns along the same path to left-side preparation while right hikite stays quiet. When the separate task ends, use lesson 8’s rear-foot-to-level exit; within KA-P1, follow its specified next unit. Step and hand are deliberately separated; returning both hands to side preparation is also this proposal’s reset. This is not a full demonstration or application acceptance of traditional oi-zuki timing.
messages.s_e79cbcff7b9da8150cdc7df038b39aec5e4df3: Write “passing foot → new forward side → hand” for each start.
messages.s_e67ca0c84ab43becb9f1081eea33bb47cad3c7: From left-forward, the right foot passed. Which hand, and when, in this preparation?
messages.s_c54303b4f87f311a38e9a04331982a0988b59d: The right hand after settling and stopping. From the opposite start, the left hand follows the left foot. Settle first, then the hand; this is separated preparation.
messages.s_80f3d478a9d2b3c84a5f4fac1399700b549878: If you wrote the opposite hand, mark the new forward foot again; retain wrist/elbow and recovery limits for the hand.
messages.s_d99beca5f8ea1c31a0b40c0cf779e12e2412bf: For both sides, draw both hands in side preparation → across-body preparation/other hand slightly forward → downward path/other hand hikite → pause → working hand up-and-back at its own side/hikite hand stays → both hands in side preparation. Label each hand’s finishing ribs and palm orientation.
messages.s_60b12f02e1a3ebc28d3de2d6a2526a6fd12510: After the left downward-path endpoint, which hand recovers along which path to where; what does the right do, and what does this not prove?
messages.s_ab93a1acbe70ad9c96fd9c952eebbcca7c4b11: The left first pauses in empty space above the left front thigh; the right is in right lower-rib hikite. Bend the left elbow comfortably at its own left side and bring the left fist on a short up-and-back path near the torso to the left lower ribs, palm comfortably toward upward; right hikite stays. Both hands return to their starting side preparations. Reverse for the right side. This proves neither contact/interception nor acceptance of the full traditional technique; recovery and palm/endpoint need P2/P5 review.
messages.s_68fe91b75049180b17825e7ffe1d2ccf80ace2: “Return the hands” alone is insufficient: add the working hand’s own side, short up-and-back path and lower-rib endpoint, and the other hikite hand staying. If you wrote leg impact, circling in front of the face, sharp shoulder pulling or successful defense, correct these to the empty-space soft endpoint and unobserved application boundary.
messages.s_2b615fcf1bb4bad083294fa92ef639f2b32196: Hide the arrows and write recovery on both sides plus both fists’ positions before the next oi-zuki. Turn uncertain orientation/path into an instructor question rather than a physical retest.
messages.s_26179fec2f0ec6a6ff5f6ca9e83be5abd16ce0: Draw N, your own right E and the intermediate direction. Number the neutral exit, four new right-left-right-left footprints and complete pause at E; do not cross the tracks. Write the leftward exit mirror separately as left-right-left-right.
messages.s_b9991a4e0b9f43aa5006b0728575217ead6f3e: In the selected walk from N to E, what is the foot order and final settlement; is rotating a loaded sole appropriate?
messages.s_cb72b503710790d928884d61d10fd1706a2c0b: First neutral exit and a pause. Two small right-left placements toward the intermediate direction, then two right-left placements toward E; the final left comes level on the left side of the right, both feet settle parallel and stop completely. Do not twist a loaded sole; lift and relocate the foot changing direction. The leftward mirror is left-right-left-right, ending with the right level to the right of the left. This original walking diagram is not acceptance of a traditional pivot.
messages.s_6777973564efe23ef64ec365a3515219bc1784: If you used mirrored right/left, a single planted-foot pivot or vague “small steps,” relabel the body directions and four foot placements. Do not use a paper diagram to authorize physical practice while personal suitability is uncertain.
messages.s_35e85604e741f40bf0c5d2d8bbea536c57f14b: Without moving the feet, recall neutral exit → right-left-right-left → stop at E, plus the leftward exit mirror.
messages.s_bcfba8eb6ec4d2c549d50ee29171c892600dcf: Draw A→B→C toward N and C→D toward E. Mark C/D turning clearance, the separate D→C W and C→A S exit, right-left-right(to level) footprints on each straight exit segment, and the N finish at A.
messages.s_1e73363dd55eedd8e7454194b202f465616c61: Are A–D targets that stack feet on one track or camera measurements?
messages.s_9fba1b5abed14f8decc9194c5b5250462c449b: No. A–D are body areas; feet use separate tracks with no measurement/score. C has neutral exit and the N→E walking turn. The sequence ends at D in neutral facing E. The separate exit is D→C W, C→A S and finally N again at A; it needs turning clearance and right-left-right(to level) on each straight segment.
messages.s_467e18e7e248a8064d1beb11089a338d78cf80: If hand paths or turning clearance do not fit, record the greater space requirement on paper; do not compress them physically.
messages.s_363cbdfd6951b05491cf41b73870b668ae8c38: Hide the plan and rewrite A, B, C, D and the N/E relationship in your own words.
messages.s_3d2d62199ddd39d5e6714f88b10b531d52ca3d: Three pauses on the first line
messages.s_3365afc1b9820c5de5189d3c475499cfdc1cb6: Unit one at A faces N in parallel preparation, hands resting at the sides, with a complete pause. Unit two: move the left foot a small amount forward on its own track, settle fully left-forward at B and stop. Bring both fists comfortably to lower-rib side preparations; then perform lesson 11’s left gedan-barai preparation and right hikite, and pause. From the empty endpoint above the left thigh, bend the left elbow comfortably and bring the left fist on the short up-and-back path at its own side to the left lower ribs, palm comfortably toward upward; the right remains in right hikite. Both hands are now in side preparation. Unit three: the right rear foot passes forward on its own right track; settle right-forward at C and stop. The right fist takes the short straight path from right-side preparation while left hikite stays quiet. After a pause, return the right along the same short path to the right lower ribs, retaining straight wrist relationship, comfortable elbow/shoulder and palm comfortably toward upward. Pause with both fists back in side preparation. These three units form an original order; retain foot–settle–hand separation. In the full sequence, lesson 15’s fourth unit follows this pause. When ending only the three-unit review, rest the hands; keep the right front foot in place and advance the left rear on its own track until level with the right, then stop in neutral. This separate exit is outside the three units; add no turn.
messages.s_79406291dbf4d94af2dd0873865ec427c76387: Write each unit’s location, forward foot, working hand and hikite hand. Add which path returns the left at B and right at C to which side of the ribs, with the other hand staying.
messages.s_c99a088c2b2be6a0860ea12a84054caf246604: At B, which hand recovers and how; at C, which new forward foot/hand works and what does the other hand do?
messages.s_4dded8e791febf1b4d6f125c6a5338c1b01e04: At B are left forward foot, left downward path and right hikite. The left returns along its short up-and-back path at its own left side to the left lower ribs; right hikite stays. The right foot then passes and settles at C; the right goes from right-side preparation on the straight path while left hikite stays, and returns along the same short path to the right lower ribs. Settle the foot first; retain both hands’ defined recovery position.
messages.s_3bbc9793c9ce133e78c0ec92e8de2eee497367: If you wrote the left hand at C, correct the same-side match. If you omitted recovery at B, add the left returning at its own side to its left ribs; do not hide the gap with an unnecessary forward movement of the other hand or rapidly joined units.
messages.s_77e46e95105da083aad34c1e3062d69042cdcc: Hide the explanation and draw the three units with both hands’ recovery paths; after consulting the key, write one concrete matching/path correction.
messages.s_fdfd59846215c1fdfe0d53c5f0c6a0f333ece7: Second line and all six units
messages.s_1568602029f390e54440715d4e00beafcca409: Hide the KA-P1 table and write the six units with hand recoveries and neutral-exit feet. Draw the separate exit as D E→S→W, right-left-right(to level) to C, C W→S left turn, right-left-right(to level) to A, then A S→W→N; label each turn’s foot order. Mark uncertainty with a question mark.
messages.s_8874eceed91d029dd3620595df0cb81f8bd7bf: After the right downward path at C, which hand recovers to where; which foot closes to neutral at D, and what is the separate return to A’s direction/foot order?
messages.s_94303fa0fb1f9963a2b544a7c261d879975a73: At C the right returns on its short up-and-back path at its own right side to the right lower ribs while left hikite stays. The left foot passes to D and settles; the left straight hand works while right hikite stays, and returns on the same path to the left lower ribs. At D rest the hands, keep the left front foot and bring the right rear foot on its own track level with the left; neutral pause facing E ends unit six/the sequence. Separate exit: two right quarters at D E→S→W; right-left-right(to level) west to C; left quarter at C W→S; right-left-right(to level) south to A; two right quarters at A S→W→N and complete pause. Right quarters are right-left-right-left; the left quarter is left-right-left-right. The exit is outside the sequence; this is not Heian/Taikyoku.
messages.s_4d3fa33c8397a8724de877c16efd8e77bd46ed: If hand recovery says only “return,” add side/path/rib endpoint. If you moved the front foot during neutral exit, correct to rear-foot-to-level order. messages.s_7e2f60a31662a89d0d60973fcaa4a8af462bb8: Correct only the confused hand/foot transition once on paper, then recall the six units and separate exit. Retain every pause and all prior P requirements.

messages.s_b487c19a71e90614d608808338fcbdeda7df86: Write separate “unattempted / uncertain / compared in writing” rows for stance, hands, stepping, turning and sequence. State the next instructor question and the named-kata gap.
messages.s_bca9e74b8d703ae36d86261a332de03fbb4c95: Which conclusion is wrong in “I know the written order; I did not attempt it physically; I learned Heian Shodan”?
messages.s_686f81941cea15c7025b67dbfd2744e7c78917: The claim to have learned Heian Shodan is wrong. The correct record is written review of original KA-P1 and physical components unattempted/unverified. There is no belt, kumite, impact or self-defense acceptance.
messages.s_0f1dd9c62da99428daee403ccea9938c866777: Separate the completion statement by component and retain the gaps. For an unobserved component, record uncertainty rather than substituting a key match.
messages.s_3d15c67d443bc0eff8f7e062990120b00ad2ea: Choose one stance and retain it through the course; stop and reset before changing it. Mirroring the sides does not verify technique. Work through lessons in order without a daily lesson target. If a prerequisite is uncertain, defer the next physical task and use its written option. “Attempted / unattempted / uncertain” is the learner's account, not a rating.

First prepare the hand seated: curl the fingers into the palm and keep the thumb outside across the curled fingers, never trapped inside the fist. Keep the wrist in line with the forearm rather than bent up/down or sideways. Avoid clenching with tension; a comfortably closed fist is enough. If fist/wrist setup is uncomfortable, use a small open-hand arm trace or written option instead of the punch task. That trace does not establish a learned jab.

Physical lead-straight prerequisites: lesson 3 stance/guard, comfortable fist/wrist setup, consistency with individual movement restrictions and understanding of the task path. From the chosen stance, the lead fist travels from near the face along an imaginary forward line; the elbow does not swing sideways. The palm may turn comfortably toward down as the arm advances; this is forearm rotation, not wrist bending. Stop short of elbow lock and return along the same path to guard; the rear hand stays near the face. Do not lean to reach or force the shoulder upward. Use two separate slow attempts. This is short-range non-contact jab practice, not power work, target impact or verified jab mastery.
messages.s_59a2269710210df1634b6885a57b01b9436687: Is the thumb outside, wrist in line with forearm and rear hand in guard? Which did I actually observe?
messages.s_9019c42330c74910a02d400dd62881e843051b: For wrong/uncertain hand setup, open the hand and re-explain setup seated; do not retry a jab until setup is comfortable and understood. For a path error alone, retain the prerequisites, shorten reach and retry one out-and-back.
messages.s_54d64296e7866b10a21f2893df9eb5b5127304: Thumb outside, wrist in line with forearm; an unobserved item is uncertain.

messages.s_973d28961fbff058eed398ba7e0286ee9f5a8a:
Prerequisites for the small turn without punching: lesson 3 stance and lessons 4–5 small-step/stop tasks were comfortable and without unresolved uncertainty; the surface permits easy foot turning, movement restrictions allow it, and an instructor has provided individual feedback on this foot–knee–hip task. That feedback is not presumed supplied. If prerequisites are unmet, explain the following sequence seated; do not substitute torso rotation over a planted foot as an easier physical task.

A small turn in guard: allow the rear heel to become light comfortably; on the forefoot, let the rear foot and knee change direction a little toward the front together as the rear hip/shoulder also move slightly forward. The knee follows the foot's direction; do not turn the knee inward over a fixed foot. Keep the lead foot in place and maintain spacing without pitching the torso forward. Do not force heel elevation or target a loading percentage. Reverse the small turn, settle the rear heel comfortably and stop. Defer physical work if the foot is blocked or the relationship is uncertain. Make one turn-only attempt, then rest.

Prerequisites for adding cross: suitable instructor feedback on the separate turn and lesson 6 comfortable fist/wrist setup. As the rear fist travels from near the face a short straight distance forward, use that same small foot–knee–hip turn; keep the lead hand in guard. Let the palm turn comfortably toward down, with wrist straight and elbow unlocked. Return the fist and torso/foot to the start, then stop. Attempt one separate cross. A seated arm trace is not equivalent to this coordination or learning cross.
messages.s_104221d5bebd179e9bf236df4f4de4ade42f35: Did the knee/torso turn without the rear foot, and did the lead hand remain in guard?
messages.s_e6f49f84c2970366558bedd4fbf0601394506a: For a blocked foot/uncertain alignment, defer physical retry, draw the sequence and ask the instructor. If only guard return was omitted, retry one smaller cross–guard only while all turn prerequisites remain satisfied.

messages.s_ea262ae9d36c4a44e29405d80a216e791cdfde: Explain lead straight → guard → rear straight → guard with four spoken cues. messages.s_ec0718adb58a544a88d95438ac5d18e38541d5:
Kicking requires individual demonstration/feedback on temporary single-leg loading; two-feet-down transfer does not establish it. Place a fixed nonsliding counter beside the chosen supporting leg, reachable without stretching, turning the torso toward it or blocking the forward kick path. The hand on that side stays on the counter; the other may remain in comfortable guard. If two hands are needed, defer this pathway's physical kick, retain both feet down for preparation/written sequencing and request an individual adaptation. Reducing support is not an endpoint requirement.

Discuss a small two-feet-down loading change with the instructor. In this non-kicking preparation, avoid locking the supporting knee and keep its direction aligned with the foot. Record supported/seated/deferred. Without demonstration and individual feedback, prerequisites for physical kicking in lessons 11–13 are unmet; written tasks remain available.

messages.s_8141176e46cf5bd30a8969ba4ef2a1bc346ebc:
Instructor prerequisite: the support/foot/landing option below must have been demonstrated for you with individual feedback; comfort alone is not permission. Begin with both feet in a comfortable stance, torso tall and facing ahead. The rear leg supports a lead-foot kick; the lead leg supports a rear-foot kick. Keep the fixed counter beside the supporting leg. Shift gradually onto that leg; its knee remains unlocked and follows the foot, with the supporting sole comfortably down. This straight-forward task has no pivot or hop. Do not force the supporting heel upward or lean the torso backward.

Lift the kicking foot a little, bringing the knee forward within a low comfortable range while the lower leg hangs downward. Replace the foot in its own prior footprint without hopping or throwing it far away to catch balance. As it settles, return comfortably to two-foot loading and stop. Lead/rear attempts are separate, with individual prerequisites applying on each side. Do not lift a foot if the supporting knee/foot relationship is uncertain. If two hands are needed, retain lesson 10's two-feet-down option.
messages.s_e2cf8c19bb5b3871e069b76c338ed58fa453b8: Which leg supported, and could I return to the prior footprint?
messages.s_6479d6741eddd6b417ed2ccb505b20d26ac3ac: Reduce height or retain both feet down. Do not retry single-leg work without the same technique prerequisites; the two-foot option is not a kick.
messages.s_b0ab1557e5ef94c316e1cc0e1e153a87f0140b: Rear leg supports lead kick, lead leg supports rear kick; return to prior footprint.
messages.s_c32b7dac7ded009a4ea7d3073a305d018c887e:
Lesson 11's individual support/landing task and instructor feedback are prerequisites. The chosen variant is a non-contact low straight-forward extension, not labeled Muay Thai teep, roundhouse or a belt standard. On the kicking foot, draw the toes comfortably up/back and use a small comfortable ankle position to face the ball of the foot forward rather than aiming the toe tips ahead. Do not force toes/ankle into that shape; defer extension if uncomfortable or uncertain. This foot shape does not establish a tested impact surface; strike nothing.

A: Establish lesson 11's small knee preparation and support. B: Extend the lower leg a short distance forward without seeking height or a fully straight knee; keep the knee unlocked and torso from leaning back. C: Before letting the foot drop, bend the knee again to return the lower leg to the small preparation. D: Lower the kicking foot gently into its prior footprint, settle the sole comfortably, return to two-foot loading and stop. Retain the supporting leg's comfortable foot/knee direction throughout and keep the supporting hand on the counter. Do not strike the floor with toes or stamp the heel. One separate attempt per side, resting on both feet between sides.
messages.s_3537f0aca9662c22331e45b7ef6e42290f896c: Did I drop from B and omit C, or need an extra step to catch balance at D?

messages.s_79ad34453bb72b7b6466fa3bdf7c5c3c40e045: Check the space before every physical lesson. If comfortable, walk slowly for 30–60 seconds or make small seated shoulder/hand movements, then use the easy stance task. These durations are suggested caps, not requirements. Begin with small range and slow speed. Do not hold or force the breath or attach it to counts; keep breathing comfortably. Pause and rest after a few attempts. Finish with comfortable walking or seated rest. Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unsafe balance or unusual discomfort; use safe support/rest and do not retry the harder task that session. Seek professional advice for continuing symptoms and urgent help for severe/sudden symptoms. This text gives no diagnosis or return-to-activity clearance. Stop after suspected head injury and seek individual health guidance [S8].
messages.s_164f02395a231b7a1aaf745567684416244444: Own side: Left/right refer to the learner, never a mirrored presenter.
messages.s_0ea95f14f4bd2527f395476e5ab2c99ef72691: Orthodox: Left foot/hand lead, right foot/hand rear.
messages.s_26fc35bb7b7750a50d2224f327d137b266564f: Southpaw: Right foot/hand lead, left foot/hand rear.
messages.s_848a7680f48b4e95c735227553fd3a3c1800c8: Lead/rear: Relative to chosen stance, not walking direction.
messages.s_3b253234b19794314b1c59f74705f00407ee31: Count: Sequence cue, not seconds, breaths or a score.
messages.s_44b57e81f9e197a9197f39db5737792738eb35: Reset: Stop first; place both feet in the comfortable chosen stance and restore guard.
messages.s_93d5a507d3ca95fc8354aea381bfa53fadd540: Supported: One/both hands on fixed support; a supporting hand does not punch.
messages.s_cb514ef18b5c7bd72b1fc4b2aed0eda17b0ec2: Seated: Fixed chair, feet down: direction, planning, small arm path; not equivalent to stepping/kicking.
messages.s_12832374d427d3a1b86ac8153a9a7baa04ac87: Muay Thai A: selected fundamentals and original paused preparation
messages.s_c8be64ff60c0ad65045217e1ed324757005bb2: Selected preparation vocabulary from contemporary Muay Thai fundamentals. Guard, base and heel use vary between sources. The short, slow, paused arrangement below is an original preparation adaptation; it is not universal camp technique or an official Khan syllabus.
messages.s_b49e6cbfd6c3bb8a85f5e0ba17edbecfa1b487: An adult beginner reader with no assumed Muay Thai experience. This is not a children’s program, rehabilitation, a medical suitability decision or competition preparation. Boxing, kickboxing or karate written lessons do not satisfy this domain’s physical prerequisites.
messages.s_41b897527c73f9f396b8288365d8359251d432: The finite A-level outcome is written recall of scope and stopping, entry to a selected stance/guard, foot order in four directions, recovery from jab and rear straight preparation, the different returns of lead teep and rear knee preparation, short horizontal elbow preparation, and original MT-P1 Nine pauses; identify one correction and plan a suitable written retest. Physical components are unattempted and unverified.
messages.s_72053ae4f2312c83fc9c8915426d7acda8e06e: Written recall does not accept technique, balance or defense. MT-P1 is an original JabLab arrangement, not a traditional form, Wai Kru/Ram Muay or official examination. Round kicks, actual check timing, clinch, catches/sweeps, contact, bag/pad work, sparring, competition and self-defense are outside this outcome. The wider complete beginner Muay Thai goal remains open.
messages.s_acb2a02f7d992510efea27e4f53c4dc5f90655: Read the text, then hide both reading and key. Write your own answer and uncertainty. messages.s_1a1d90c8a7650f82eed3da0daf3cc5d0ac4988: The paper example is left foot forward, right foot back, facing the same forward direction: F=left lead foot/hand, R=right rear foot/hand. Each foot stays on its own side rail. F0/R0 is home; F1/R1 is the base moved forward by the same small distance. In a right-leading mirrored example F=right and R=left; lateral movement starts with the foot on the movement side. Physical stance choice is not automatically inferred from handedness; stance switching is not taught.
messages.s_2a6bb455ecc766af882a1bbc435d0da21ed839: 1 · N→F0/R0 · Left stays, right steps briefly back on its own rail; both hands to own guard through mt-04 open hand→curl four fingers→lay thumb outside. Same forward facing; pause in two-foot base.
messages.s_4d0eb40303397477cf0f9ad4beb70c7452f140: 2 · F0/R0→F1/R1 · Left first to F1, right second to R1; same small distance, guard and rails retained. Pause.
messages.s_101d25912fd4c1cc3cddb131bb11df963b2ea9: 3 · F1/R1 · Short left jab→same-path left guard; right guard retained, feet stay. Pause.
messages.s_df73e0652d220669624592aa80632a53e9e88e: 4 · F1/R1 · Right rear straight→right guard and small heel/hip/shoulder unwind; left guard retained, both feet at initial directions. Pause.
messages.s_7927152ad9677934b6cda3ddd129596096d932: 5 · F1/R1 · Load transfers from two feet to right R1, left unloads; low bent left knee, ball forward/toes back-up→brief extend→re-bend→ground own F1→reload both feet. Retain right R1 and both guards. Pause.
messages.s_dff60b496727d9410c7caf6676cbe8e975b61e: 6 · F1/R1 · Load transfers from two feet to left F1, right unloads; short bent right knee/folded lower leg→back-down to ground own R1→reload both feet. Retain left F1 and both guards. Pause.
messages.s_93701196b22aba7b454059fb294e69e3841e2d: 7 · F1/R1 · Short right horizontal elbow→retrace the same arc to own right side, right guard and heel unwind; left guard retained. Pause.
messages.s_b59c64a2659fc027a2516c88a3ee28ced43986: 8 · F1/R1→F0/R0 · Backward right to R0 first, left to F0 second; guard and side rails retained. Pause.
messages.s_51189540e1a49f76d7e0d1f8d4cbe36a3fdea1: 9 · F0/R0→N · Hands return to rest on own side paths; release the external thumb, then open four fingers. Left F0 stays; right advances on its own rail only to left level. Stop at parallel N; sequence ends.
messages.s_b329844202b99b632e0fab579bdeaf930affae: Muay Thai is a distinct domain with elbow, knee and kick families alongside punches. Cultural context and respect for teachers matter. Recognizing the name Wai Kru/Ram Muay does not teach its performance. This proposal reviews selected preparations in writing; finishing prior kickboxing lessons does not open the whole Muay Thai domain. Start by recording what you do not know.

messages.s_ccc94173e7bed98b85610191a94fc639859e9d: If the reader cannot explain teep recovery, should they repeat faster, and what should they record?
messages.s_81eca3da56ee323ec1044ae2d6ce5f014ee9c2: Record the recovery uncertainty, stop the task and seek clarification. Speed does not replace correct recovery or actual observation. Physical practice stays unavailable.
messages.s_f86816dfe3fc745bd6433da29aa14857008be1: Do not erase the uncertainty row with the correct answer; separately name what needs review.
messages.s_37bafbb8d32e420d15b97e177cf2babf68c239: Answer the same scenario unaided in a later written session; add no physical task.
messages.s_f9a2adc06df1ed25352b480133f309926676a6: Entering stance and exiting to neutral
messages.s_5745455de721a13009507d639ee31b4f9b7a35: On paper start at N, a comfortable parallel-foot rest position. The left foot stays; the right is placed a short step back on its own right rail at R0, leaving the left at F0, facing the same forward direction. Knees are not locked; width, foot direction, heels and loading need personal review, with no prescribed percentage or angle. To exit, rest both hands; F0 stays and the R0 foot advances on its own rail to level with the left, then stops at parallel N. This lift-and-place path is not a standard for every source stance.
messages.s_3ee96f0c0f4d4a021c61e846b637b8abb7557e: P0 and P1 are unmet. Trace stance and the return to N on paper only.
messages.s_4e3879ef1d92dc22f7d9c4e2ca82874f98aa21: Draw N→F0/R0→N and name the moving and stationary foot on each arrow.
messages.s_f6349271643c43915931d88d50e5a231b80293: In the left-leading example, does exit pull the left foot back or pass the right foot ahead of it?
messages.s_3d8f691b6b3319d4adc54c2e0e6d1a55b6379f: Neither. Hands rest; left F0 stays and right R0 advances on its own right rail only to level with it; both stop at parallel N. In the right-leading mirror, the right lead stays and the left rear comes level on its own rail.
messages.s_7e82fbfc6d2da045a1a00fdf3391fee70a285d: Keep lateral width in the drawing; add no crossing onto one line or pivot to achieve alignment.
messages.s_165b59c84fc0a428a47636b3910a93f947b635: Redraw entry and exit with reading hidden; check the foot’s start and end separately.
messages.s_ca196d63fefa33e5aed8ebd322fe2d2f488615: Establish F0/R0 on paper. The resting hand is comfortably open. To form the fist, keep the thumb outside while curling the middle and end joints of the other four fingers toward the palm until the fingertips rest in it. Then lay the thumb across the outside of the curled index and middle fingers; do not trap it inside or leave it sticking sideways. Keep the wrist in the forearm line without bending; this noncontact preparation adds no forceful squeezing. Raise each hand along its own short side path to guard beside the face; palms face each other in this example. Do not force elbows outward or clamp them to the trunk; retain vision and a comfortable head position. To exit, lower each hand on the same own-side path to rest, release the thumb from the outer fingers, then open the four fingers. Source differences in palm direction/height make no guard universal or impact-proof.
messages.s_8249a40015b469007e32001754550cc36a9ce7: P0/P1 are unmet; do not physically try the hand or guard position.
messages.s_2c13492b07a2e59600c58542a86bf08c0f9715: Draw four frames: open hand→curl four fingers→external thumb and straight wrist→own guard path. Write the return to rest and opening order; separately record uncertainty about vision and palm direction.
messages.s_93653365b03d2af949c413143cf2492d0b6f7e: Does tucking the thumb into the palm first and closing the other fingers over it match this fist example? Write the closure/opening order. Can source majority alone accept a guard with a different palm direction?
messages.s_8b19b946100b9ef71352ee76c9a74e00d7d2cd: No. Curl the four fingers into the palm while keeping the thumb outside, then lay the thumb across the outside of index/middle fingers. The wrist continues the forearm line. Hands travel to their own guard and back along the same path to rest; release the thumb before opening the four fingers. Guard examples vary by context; source majority proves neither vision, hand formation nor physical acceptance.
messages.s_ce30bb082275ef4c105c0861c84ddac547c13c: Correct the trapped thumb to one held outside first and then laid across the curled fingers. Add any missing four-finger curl or opening order; remove a universal-guard claim.
messages.s_6a5d2368787eba97d461fb73065de139548f8b: In a later written session describe open hand, closure, own guard and reopening at rest without the key; record uncertainty about thumb, wrist and vision. Add no form-validation claim.
messages.s_9f228ae1fa0e89e3d398eb0a73f3f0a614cf47: Start on paper with left-leading F0/R0 and guard. Forward: place left F0 a small distance along its own rail at F1, then move right R0 the same distance to R1 and pause. Backward: place right R1 at R0 first, then bring left F1 to F0 and pause. The lead remains lead and rails do not cross; feet do not slide or jump together. This paused lift-and-place example is not dynamic ring footwork. Do not solve insufficient space with a bigger step or a stumbling retreat.
messages.s_2a7db37860056cfe0edd4e09f7a3ebfa7daf48: P0–P2 are unmet; forward/backward steps are not performed physically.
messages.s_847ebfa4147c4d06af43c53b63e33a995987cd: Draw the four foot placements in numbered order and write the base after each pair.
messages.s_85a0f5695d52331a188de945e0f3f352462851: What is the foot order when the left-leading example advances and returns to the same base?
messages.s_2008327946038eb1607304fe833dc5961d83b5: Left F0→F1, right R0→R1; pause. Right R1→R0, left F1→F0; pause. Left remains lead, lateral width is retained, and physical balance is not verified.
messages.s_dcb4968691c0812bf342f41307f8f766bec3c9: Correct a drawing with rear-first forward movement or lead-first backward movement; retain the intermediate base.
messages.s_f48105ef7c60b402d6a86162b9868cd312db11: Retest only the erroneous direction’s two placements in writing, then check the full four placements.
messages.s_ba6a32f4aabcd8572765fef18b10321e709c26: Moving sideways and returning to the same place
messages.s_cd8f067a871f0c22d994d18c3f3e74ec3463c3: In the left-leading F0/R0 example keep facing forward. To move right, place the right foot the same small distance right on its own side, then let the left follow that distance and pause. To return left, place the left at old F0 first and the right at old R0 second. For an initial move left, left goes first and right follows; return right is right first, left second. Feet do not pass each other at any intermediate placement. Moving right differs from turning to face right; add no pivot or stance switch.
messages.s_287d4d8a2a8d21d02f1f3946a484fc3c3623a1: P0–P2 are unmet; the lateral path exists on paper only.
messages.s_4224113906bba18fd925e726bc44f857212551: Write separate four-placement lists for right-and-back and left-and-back; label movement and facing directions separately.
messages.s_e919aa403139aa07522159207bf96fc869b28c: In a left-leading stance does the left lead always start a move right?
messages.s_e1eca61e37a8647f7c948ce89ab2535b9f3573: No. Rightward is right then left; return left is left then right. Leftward is left then right; return right is right then left. “Lead first” applies to forward movement, not every direction; facing stays forward.
messages.s_0f7f5705ca342cce8c40e945774ac2be22da15: Choose the right/left foot on the lateral movement side rather than lead/rear; remove an arrow that passes the other foot.
messages.s_535c1b05b6b90bdfa2495fb53561b2acc2c0fa: Explain unaided that in a right-leading paper example rightward still starts right and leftward starts left.
messages.s_b17f73c2f7d42ab3039303434460fe3eca9df6: Jab: extension and return to own guard
messages.s_fb3b970e363868884b6174840c9810806ac759: With left-leading F0/R0 and both hands in guard, extend the left lead fist briefly and slowly along its own forward lane without drawing it back to load. The right stays at its own guard location. The wrist continues the forearm line and the elbow does not lock. Any comfortable forearm/palm rotation is only the amount in an accepted demonstration. Bend the left elbow again as the fist retraces the short lane to left guard and the palm returns to its starting direction. Both feet stay, facing forward. This example adds no step, snap or target contact.
messages.s_a4bb4ca44fad3bc9021793b1a2b8c42116115d: P0/P1/P3 are unmet; no jab movement is performed.
messages.s_60d9eb4a714c9638583811361a54c7d09e2efa: Write left hand start→short extension→same-path guard return, plus the right hand and feet’s state.
messages.s_09e0d6183bd4d9f2819792f8e5a62e276defd4: Does returning the left fist in a low circle or dropping the right hand match this example’s jab recovery?
messages.s_5a01335d7b61671ed5d4e395828ef99bb20152: No. Bend the left elbow; return the left fist along its own short straight path to left guard and the palm to its starting direction. The right stays at guard and feet do not relocate. This written sequence does not accept technique or defense.
messages.s_0d259d19a3cc7dad0c72818ee9f9566be34a1c: Correct the return path in your own words without copying the key; include the inactive right hand’s location.
messages.s_8acfee0c5c60d55724f6517bce61265c1732a7: In a later written session recall left recovery and right guard without the key; do not count a remaining error as complete.
messages.s_1dc73b80e13bdd57ca8b933b6b2cb06a7369c4: Rear straight: coordinated turn and unwind
messages.s_65898ff2aaa23867feb0f4baa8eae9934f3d86: At left-leading F0/R0 with guard, extend the right rear fist along its short straight lane while right shoulder and hip move slightly forward together; in an accepted personal demonstration the right heel releases comfortably over the forefoot and turns outward to the right. The right knee follows the comfortable foot direction; do not pin the foot and force the knee around. Left hand stays at guard and left foot does not relocate. As the right elbow bends and fist returns to right guard, shoulder/hip unwind the same small motion to the start; right heel and foot direction return together to their initial R0 position. The palm returns to its comfortable starting direction. Add no step, forward fall or fixed angle.
messages.s_5de25ae44204cf5a1f497344ab3613fe03799d: P0/P1/P3 are unmet. Do not attempt heel/knee coordination and recovery without physical demonstration.
messages.s_efed07a40285acd9a008cc56b459418c04a668: Write a start–extension–return table for right hand, right heel, hip/shoulder and left guard.
messages.s_dcd21d477d1ecfe128edbed8406792962a37ed: If the right hand returns but heel/hip remain in the extended position, is recovery complete?
messages.s_a3647681f5345adbadebf23dcf7b090fd50bb8: No. As the right fist returns to right guard, unwind the small shoulder/hip movement and restore right heel/foot to their initial R0 direction together; left hand stays at guard and left foot stays. A forced planted pivot or hand-only return is not this example’s full recovery.
messages.s_12714785734cd1aa8669e5ae3b83558157377b: Add the missing lower/upper body component to the return row; invent no angle or power number.
messages.s_2b4de81dc83a43f76e83a8d38d372cf62647c8: Compare all four components’ starts and returns in a later written session; add no physical acceptance record.
messages.s_74947d287d3dd45ea8439680225d2da5d1a865: From left-leading F0/R0 and guard, trace only the mt-07 jab first: brief left extension, right guard retained, left returned to its own guard. Pause after both hands and base are restored. Then trace mt-08 rear-straight hand/heel/hip/shoulder coordination and full unwind; both hands are back at guard and F0/R0 regain their initial foot directions. Do not leave the first hand extended to start the second. These separate preparations do not establish competition one-two timing, reaction or reaching a target.
messages.s_48779b37aab88990b9dace30b71f6fb7a23e40: P0/P1/P3 are unmet; the two preparations are not physically combined.
messages.s_f1018c281b2a9ef0912f1ac40bd349a710f633: Insert a guard/base check row between jab recovery and rear-straight recovery.
messages.s_46aa3d10b1ed308a5ba8e76f08e9d1aa95730b: If the right hand starts while the left remains extended, does this arrangement retain its intermediate pause?
messages.s_70e3fe5e57c171b08952902a5f7b36089f505c: No. First restore left guard and retain F0/R0; pause. Then use the right rear straight and coordinated unwind, returning right guard and heel/hip to the start. Fluent combinations and actual timing are not accepted.
messages.s_d00ca449993ae4bc705e1f78c9ac1ad1c599cc: Add the omitted check pause; do not substitute a count of two punches for a technique outcome.
messages.s_eed0d04c763502000f30d20d99d71a93c3a305: At the next written session, order the two separate returns and intermediate base unaided.
messages.s_512b612b6aadc017407199e93223a6b19340fc: Lifting and replacing the lead leg
messages.s_58eee70cf5cc87c4f793caa47484fb825c5bd0: Before a full teep strike, describe load transfer, lifting and recovery separately. Start left-leading at F0/R0 with both feet grounded, both hands at guard and weight shared by the two feet. Without relocating either foot, keep the trunk upright and move the weight-bearing alignment of hips and trunk over the right rear foot: the right leg takes the load as the left foot unloads. This is an actual transfer, rather than merely naming the right knee “support.” Keep the support knee unlocked and avoid leaning the trunk backward. After the left foot unloads, raise the bent left knee through a comfortable low range; the foot remains free beneath it, with no kick extension. Lower that knee and place the left foot on its own left rail at old F0. Once it is grounded, share the load across both feet again and pause in guard and two-foot base. Right stays at R0; add no hopping, rail change or invented acceptance by holding something. This is a written start–action–return description; personal support demonstration and observation are separate requirements.
messages.s_d2c85a02009e03e8e95b4946a4e11d85c6fc4b: P0/P1/P4 are unmet; single-leg support and lifting are not tried.
messages.s_416974601915253f458153225af3ee31420c5d: Draw four frames: two-foot F0/R0→load transfers to right R0 and left unloads→bent left knee lifts→left F0 grounds and load returns to both feet. State both guards and the absence of extension.
messages.s_e07516080b2772c38366a5ad1ef92e92574610: Does writing “right support” while leaving weight on the left lead foot explain the start of its lift? May the left foot land farther forward? Write the initial load, transfer before lifting and recovery load.
messages.s_0ddfdc9901e9dbf0498dcff0320ce6e217400c: No. Initial load is shared by two feet. First, with feet retained, the upright trunk/hip weight-bearing alignment moves over right R0; right takes the load and left unloads. Then the bent left knee lifts without extension. The left foot returns to its own F0 and grounds before load is shared across both feet again; both hands stay at guard. A lift accepts no kick, check or balance skill.
messages.s_12e8e3b53588c95755af8edcf646fe720ed818: Replace a bare “right support” label with the phase that transfers load from two feet to right and unloads left. Correct forward landing to F0 return; restore two-foot loading only once left is grounded.
messages.s_0ade1f92618ac0586d904905129ec906216bb5: In a later written session recall initial load, transfer to right, left lift and two-foot reloading at F0 without the key. Name support and replacement feet separately; add no physical trial.
messages.s_c1e817476c3eb7f735a8ed0383867d30f6a9d8: Start left-leading at F0/R0, both feet grounded, load shared across them and both hands at guard. As in mt-10, retain the feet and move the upright trunk/hip weight-bearing alignment over right R0; once left unloads, lift its knee into a low bent chamber. Set the left ankle to present the padded sole area beneath the toe bases forward: the ball of the foot. Draw the toes backward/upward toward the shin rather than pointing their tips forward or downward. This defines direction, not a measured angle; do not force the toes. As the knee opens comfortably, the foot travels briefly forward in this arrangement; no knee lock, hip thrust or right-support relocation. There is no contact target. To return, re-bend the left knee first and withdraw the foot beneath it; then, while lowering, release foot/toes into a comfortable landing arrangement and ground the left foot at old F0. Once grounded, share load across both feet again and pause in the initial base with both guards. This original low preparation keeps both hands up; it does not adopt source arm swing, high chamber or power/contact teaching.
messages.s_4e96a5b8a4776e5eb65f33cc88cefddc805e9b: P0/P1/P4 are unmet; teep practice is unavailable. Accepted demonstrations of lifting, foot arrangement and recovery are absent.
messages.s_553c486f45843f0131a5ac5bcc9f5308d08128: Write initial load and transfer to right. Draw low bent left knee→ball forward/toes back-up→brief extension→re-bend→comfortable left F0 landing and two-foot reloading; state right R0 and both guards.
messages.s_adecb65043e5039c7e2560c5b8ac52753d3ac8: Do toes pointed forward-down and dropping the extended left leg straight to the floor match this example? Write transfer to right support, ball/toe direction and return-to-ground order.
messages.s_8732bee6d6f366b98c36db8a810cd6474a9e0d: No. Transfer two-foot load to right R0 and unload left before raising its low bent knee. Present the ball forward with toes drawn back/up toward the shin, rather than presenting forward-down toe tips. After brief extension, re-bend first and withdraw the foot beneath the knee; then release foot/toes for a comfortable landing at old left F0. Ground it before sharing load across both feet again. Retain right R0 and both guards; add no forward step, snap or contact.
messages.s_e86a7df7bd1346733762a984302b0143c81184: Replace vague “sole forward” with ball forward/toes back-up. Add missing transfer to right support; correct a straight extended-leg landing to re-bend→own F0 grounding→two-foot reloading.
messages.s_ccd51ff12759a5eab209cb6a12653d0e21ceb0: In a later written session explain start, transfer to right, ball/toe direction, brief extension and complete return without the key. Record each uncertainty; correct writing does not accept a physical teep.
messages.s_c7ed51fb7c7706ba173910baef4a6157ff7787: Rear straight-knee preparation: recovery differs from a kick
messages.s_5adda1955d8b305716ba2cbe2e9d40b8ff2680: Start left-leading at F0/R0 with both feet grounded, weight shared across them and both hands at guard. This original short preparation adds no forward step: retain foot locations and move the upright trunk/hip weight-bearing alignment over left lead F0. The left leg takes the load and right rear foot unloads; keep the support knee unlocked. After right unloads, bend the right knee through a low, brief forward-up path; the lower leg stays folded back beneath it rather than extending like a kick. Foot/toes stay comfortable; add no forced pointing, backward lean or hip thrust. Retrace that short back-down knee path and ground the right foot on its own right rail at old rear R0, while left stays at F0. After right grounds, share load across both feet again and pause in the initial base with both guards. Lead lift/teep transfers load to right; this rear-knee preparation transfers it to left. Ground the returning foot before starting the next movement. This teaches neither a full contact knee nor clinch pulling.
messages.s_328d95ff7b6aaf690b5390a6d2fb387ad06189: P0/P1/P5 are unmet; no physical knee preparation is tried.
messages.s_be116549f497fec0d165160b38bf2f92b90338: Draw separate two-foot→right loading/left F0 return for lead lift/teep and two-foot→left loading/right R0 return for rear knee. State which foot unloads, the lower-leg condition and when load returns to both feet.
messages.s_064efd676d61121f31502f0d89ac9410ef7803: If weight remains on right while the right rear knee lifts, the lower leg extends like a kick and right lands ahead of left, does that describe this preparation’s start/return? Write the correct transfer and rear return.
messages.s_7b3e435361beb9dd464d9d6dd665ef27d76b33: No. Start with two-foot loading; retain feet while moving the upright trunk/hip weight-bearing alignment over left F0 so left takes the load and right unloads. Then the right knee rises briefly while bent, with its lower leg folded. Bring the knee back-down and ground right at its own old rear R0. Only after grounding share load across both feet again; retain left F0 and both guards. Lead teep differs: right supports and left returns to F0.
messages.s_a09c2c486c00dcba9e7736e5f334db4d4fa8df: Add actual transfer to left before the right rear lift; correct an extended lower leg to folded knee preparation. Replace vague “lower” for right with grounding at old rear R0, followed by two-foot reloading.
messages.s_3a1b20157e5db9e917acf7e7a138a3ae034762: In a later written session recall unaided the opposite support transfers, distinct lower-leg phases, own return locations and two-foot reloading for lead teep/rear knee; mark no physical acceptance.
messages.s_d290516a450140d05fd88fc266da5cd02c4b0d: Short horizontal rear elbow and return to own guard
messages.s_32690e741fa33cbd2a70e6294528b0d27a7dbc: Start left-leading at F0/R0 and guard. Keep the right elbow bent while bringing the right fist near its own right shoulder at a comfortable preparation location without crossing the face; left hand retains its own left guard. With the personally demonstrated small heel/hip/shoulder coordination from mt-08, trace a short horizontal arc with the right elbow from the right side into empty space ahead; add no swing beyond the trunk’s center, target, step or contact. As the right elbow retraces that arc to its own right side, unwind the small turn and restore heel to its initial R0 direction; open the arm only enough to return the hand to right guard. Left hand/foot stay, both hands regain initial guard; pause. Contact with own face or opposite hand is a separate error needing demonstration/observation.
messages.s_63d3fe2aa93b1adfc5c951546681155a04c8b5: P0/P1/P3/P6 are unmet; no elbow preparation is performed. Do not direct it toward a person, wall or bag.
messages.s_e1d22fd03b818c0ba48101883399a751c8b637: Write three rows for right hand/elbow arc, left guard and right heel recovery; include the empty-space, no-contact limit.
messages.s_66c64aafe6f353e68d652ffe0e7303c8196d29: If the right elbow returns but the right fist stays at the shoulder and the left drops, has the example’s guard been restored?
messages.s_629704c41ca171007edb81e7545814656050c2: No. Return the right elbow arc to its own side, unwind turn/heel and restore right fist to its own right guard; left stays at its own left guard. Finishing the elbow arc alone does not complete hand/guard recovery or physical acceptance.
messages.s_9ddb15ce1629a41396ed1d7a2c7a526ab01547: Add the working right fist’s end location and inactive left hand’s location; draw no arc through the face.
messages.s_25a719356b994c0f2a827235d5c1caa6f02092: In a later written session explain start–arc–hand/heel recovery–pause without the key.
messages.s_0b4e9c259e44a20279f0a8d5e30588deced80d: Check and clinch: distinction between knowing and performing
messages.s_b35e2cc874ecc342c24ed5214552a1b648406c: A check needs a response at the appropriate time/place to an incoming kick; lifting a leg in the text does not demonstrate that timing. Clinch concerns another person’s grip, balance and contact; imaginary gripping in the air does not validate clinch control. This lesson selects no physical movement for either; do not relabel mt-10/11/12 as a check or clinch knee technique. Source partner, impact and tactical examples do not transfer to this text’s acceptance. Moving to the next selected written sequence does not open defense or clinch.
messages.s_10dbcbc0aa724f801d38a97efc27e18afe83ed: No physical task is assigned. Checks, clinch grips, neck pulling, sweeps and partner trials are not selected.
messages.s_e1ffa54de24749793a3538bedf3b29d6d95389: Write separate records for leg-path written recall, observed incoming-kick timing and actual grip feedback.
messages.s_a84a3a94b713b415e440b9a768a96691df3e01: Does correctly answering the MT-P1 key prove defense/check or clinch skill?
messages.s_48b02d46575f2ffe04de9fdcddc041a1eb5842: No. A written key match is not actual reaction, contact, partner balance or instructor feedback. Checks and clinch are physically unattempted and unverified in this course.
messages.s_57318cf5174f0c19575dd93018396d822d47d2: Do not write a solo leg lift as observation of an incoming kick; keep the missing reaction and contact records explicit.
messages.s_6df88ca92565f01dd675f05a3514b5aa67bcc8: In a later written session write each skill’s missing actual observation unaided in one sentence.
messages.s_a75a26f025834bf3449ed0a08bd535506b6e1a: MT-P1 Nine pauses: original written arrangement
messages.s_f2e921f96a249c43260cbbcc0b75a62557d4b0: MT-P1 stays facing the same forward direction on paper. 1 Enter mt-03 F0/R0 and guard with mt-04 finger closure from N. 2 Mt-05 forward left F0→F1, right R0→R1; pause. 3 Mt-07 left jab and left guard return; pause. 4 Mt-08 right rear straight, right guard and heel/hip unwind; pause. 5 Mt-11 low left teep: transfer two-foot load to right R1, unload left; low bent knee, ball forward/toes back-up, brief extension, re-bend and comfortable left F1 landing; then reload both feet and pause with both guards. 6 Mt-12 short right knee: first transfer two-foot load to left F1 and unload right; bent knee/folded lower leg, back-down grounding at right R1, then reload both feet; pause with both guards. 7 Mt-13 short right horizontal elbow, right guard and heel unwind; retain left guard; pause. 8 Mt-05 backward right R1→R0, left F1→F0; pause. 9 As in mt-04, return hands to rest on own side paths, release the external thumb and open four fingers; keep left lead F0, advance right R0 on its own rail to left level; finish at parallel N. Start each movement only after restoring the prior two-foot base, loading and guard. This is neither a universal combination nor a traditional form.
messages.s_ae00d364b0b249998fdaaacc8957ba6825bb2b: All P0–P7 are unmet; the full sequence is not performed physically. Component acceptance alone does not accept every transition.
messages.s_7d97203de9990bfc8e66f0982711c19290d89d: Hide reading and the order table; write all nine units in your own words. Include hand closure/opening, which foot takes load before 5 and 6, teep ball/toe direction, every hand/foot return, two-foot reloading and final N.
messages.s_aab48a7a2252d84b76d45d27490ecfc04bb191: In 5 load stays on left, toes point forward and left lands farther forward. In 6 load stays on right and right becomes lead; left starts backward. Is this the same arrangement? Write correct support, ball/toe arrangement, recovery base and hand closure/opening order.
messages.s_f4eebe435355aa7790109ed97939bcd6105d8c: No. In 1 curl four fingers, lay the thumb outside and bring hands to own guard. Before 5 transfer load to right R1; left unloads, briefly extends with ball forward/toes back-up, re-bends and grounds at left F1, then reload both feet. Before 6 transfer load to left F1; right unloads, performs the short knee with folded lower leg and returns to rear right R1, then reload both feet. Retain both guards. Unit 7 restores that base/guard. Unit 8 is backward right R1→R0 then left F1→F0. In 9 hands return to rest on own paths; release the external thumb and open four fingers; left F0 stays, right comes level on its own rail; finish N. A key match does not accept the whole physical sequence.
messages.s_9d25e04f52d42a1ed87a912af6da92de4e150d: Replace incorrect hand closure, support transfer in 5/6 or teep toe direction with the correct phases. Add missing grounding and two-foot reloading; keep the order paused. Choose one error and write your own correction.

messages.s_4b3bb62904f3fd18ec34c137db90637b4865c4: With reading, order table and key closed, write your own recall first. Then compare with the key and add your own correction for one error plus a later written retest. Retain “unattempted/unverified” for every physical component. Even if all answers match, record no mastery, actual balance, defense or cultural performance acceptance.

Walk the perimeter, extend one arm slowly, then make two easy steps in each direction without touching an object.

messages.s_8dc992e7c5c052cef02aa719f0ed4716d74757: Begin with a shorter seated orientation or smaller steps if standing practice is difficult; a clinician can advise on condition-specific limits.
messages.s_a6da735c220b05c1d3e98ebff378a09ddd7a98: Stop if the floor feels unsafe, you feel dizzy, or you develop chest pain or unusual breathlessness.

messages.s_2b5259624a90559e9e15bab575f766226e1343:
Hold each side for three relaxed breaths, then step out and rebuild the same stance five times.

Short focused practice: In two of the existing five rebuilds focus only on foot spacing, in two only on a calm stop, and choose one focus yourself for the last. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

messages.s_16570978fd800f4a0edb2a4e036fb60d2b16d5: Use a shorter stance or hold a wall during orientation; avoid a stance width that causes discomfort.
messages.s_35e1516fcf20e0fa490558d06d08006ffb1241: Stop if the stance causes joint pain or you cannot keep balance in the available space.
messages.s_a850dc6ceebbdd215ad774ad4d151c4ef8f246: Original front and side silhouettes show foot separation and neutral balance, without numerical angle labels.
messages.s_62a87616c4418f1c1ffb9c12614495a66d6f6b: Keep both hands available without stiffening the shoulders.

messages.s_a9a22a22cca960d98be62c5d2181e2b86995d3: Bring the rear hand near the cheek and the lead hand slightly ahead. Keep elbows comfortably toward the ribs and eyes forward.
messages.s_031380ea98a1c1ff7e352d45a2380cea535fef: Release the shoulders and hands between repetitions. A guard is a movable starting place, not a frozen pose.
messages.s_da08a31fd18bf3ec589eb8fa0ad70b77385907: Do not freeze the guard by raising the shoulders and squeezing the hands. Soften the hands, release the shoulders and check the comfortable field of view again.
messages.s_3a977acacde549f5c281b3bb86ba14444fdd45:
Raise the guard, lower it, and rebuild it ten slow times. Turn slightly side-on while keeping both hands visible to yourself.

Short focused practice: Split the existing ten guard rebuilds into two short groups and lower the hands to check comfort between them. In the last two focus only on the rear hand returning to its ready place. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Rebuild the guard after a small side step and retain the same comfortable view.

Next practice: At the next suitable session, recall the short sequence without reading first. Briefly revisit Find your stance; check only the confusing part again.
messages.s_2fb07c7754a8ff764caf9c7bb73b043e561363: I can see ahead without hiding behind my gloves.
messages.s_32980178055d74ada045b80c27aff8e6ca2850: My shoulders can relax while the hands remain ready.
messages.s_0d0828d913e9a89a2d2147d8d92797b76b13a0: I can rebuild a comfortable guard and relax the shoulders while the hands are ready.
messages.s_03d8752a7ee33882f9f914e87f1d585429aa80: Lower the hands between sets or shorten the hold if shoulders tire; choose a comfortable range with a qualified coach if needed.
messages.s_78354bc79215b53576611b1d45a8c560dfa5f4: Stop for sharp shoulder, elbow or wrist pain; fatigue is not a reason to force the guard higher.
messages.s_50750b05e3ac0693a96f190304da1e27d07504: Original three-quarter view: begin with a close-up of the thumb outside softly curled fingers and comfortable wrist, then show hands, elbows and sightline with relaxed shoulders. No impact demonstration.
messages.s_b97c988e3d1c11ad3ad7920626029d320af39a: Move and breathe without holding the breath during effort.
messages.s_56c547c0ae91c0ada2a54788419a805249ba43: Take an ordinary breath while settling in guard; exhale gently as one hand extends and breathe again on the return.
messages.s_27a2b7968e4a817a2553d3475140ae2270cb41: Keep a pace at which you could still speak a short sentence. This is preparation, not a speed test.
messages.s_14acc7471dab9cbf7402d6802dc1bb15018d28: Do not hold the breath to keep up or force a hard exhale on every movement. Reduce the reach and return to ordinary breathing and a comfortable conversational pace.
messages.s_196fef942a22a109a427b345e9f7c51cdc019a:
Alternate ten tiny hand reaches with easy breathing; rest whenever you need it.

Short focused practice: During the first five existing small reaches focus only on easy breathing, then stop and say a short sentence. Reduce or omit the remaining reaches if needed. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Carry the easy-breathing focus into a separate attempt with a small step.

Next practice: At the next suitable session, recall the short sequence without reading first. Briefly revisit A relaxed guard; check only the confusing part again.
messages.s_68e77c7c3a2c36396a94368e43c6cd91ee5438: I did not hold my breath to finish a reach.

messages.s_07d5e8c2b0ffad03d6063b6ba92d57fb631725: Reduce the number of reaches or practise breathing in a supported stance; seek condition-specific advice before exertion when appropriate.
messages.s_48eec00f77f7c827d9433c662dcb9fe47d793e: Stop if breathing feels unusually difficult, you feel faint, or chest discomfort appears.
messages.s_16dc4ca292ba9ca9dfbf4ee8359b13a1c6a509: Original close and wide alternation: gentle exhale with one reach, visible pause, no speed meter.
messages.s_cc01cc518d7a6987382ae5245c8b503aa0ca4c: Recover the same stance and guard after each small movement.
messages.s_c203373479af9861a2ca2200f23be7bef7eb69: From guard, step a little to one side, stop, check the space between your feet, then bring the hands back to their ready place.
messages.s_95538e7ebfd8e03ef0da040bb81b380a8a16ad: Repeat on both sides. Keep each reset unhurried; later punches will end in this base.
messages.s_62407813c65e952889f92426488e33a5221127: Do not skip checking the base before the next movement. Check foot spacing first, then the hands' return to their ready place.
messages.s_5c5d3699340ba17afa67627b2be90e82b70513:
Make five small side steps each way with a full pause and reset after every step.

Short focused practice: Say step-stop-feet-hands for the first two of the existing five steps each way; recall the same order privately for the remainder. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Choose the same reset after a small back step rather than a side step.

Next practice: At the next suitable session, recall the short sequence without reading first. Briefly revisit Find your stance; check only the confusing part again.
messages.s_fe8f32739ab0c3469bdfb087ea2d3672d4de62: I can pause without crossing my feet.
messages.s_01b5740baab1dc1cdb77e001bfbe508f91adcc: Both hands return before I start the next step.
messages.s_7306d42a0a518718655c4894b61882a26e3ebe: I can prepare the feet and hands again without rushing after a side step.
messages.s_1673482448f12bb0c20a472e2f241ddd04c76e: Use only a weight shift if stepping is uncomfortable; keep support close during early practice.
messages.s_6bebecb0988d78bc7f1629480bad2fdac8492e: Stop if resetting requires a sudden catch step or causes pain.
messages.s_a3534b8d87e1330a6dd1cc1c5ac8ae19fc498e: Original wide front view with a pause frame after each step; highlight foot spacing and hand return.
messages.s_481011e9665b398f9edd1d8b7a896153aae2e7: Learn small steps before adding punches; the feet return to a usable stance after every move.
messages.s_6fa009423642c9ef45ccc20ed69253ebcd9b01: Move in either direction without narrowing or crossing the stance.
messages.s_90f444b0a8c56aa9a0fd0707aded9129375fed: Forward: lead foot starts, rear foot follows. Backward: rear foot starts, lead foot follows. Keep the step small enough to stop midway.
messages.s_7f2450c03f075f7829a564e17d510b8d127ef2: Pause after each pair of steps and check your original foot spacing. Speed comes after you can stop balanced.
messages.s_21a40383c6f2ea1763295e7c840e22e9a948e6: Do not bring the following foot against the first and erase the base. Take a small first step, then follow only enough to restore the starting spacing.
messages.s_1e2039d6b9cea0184787a2143c9ebc79ee29ee:
Trace a short line on the floor mentally: five forward-follow steps, five backward-follow steps, each with a pause.

Short focused practice: For the existing forward-back steps, pause through the first two pairs each way and name the initiating foot; recall the direction choice yourself in the last pair. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Swap the forward-back pairs and choose the first foot yourself before starting.

messages.s_f84f06324361db281835cbefe82531462aa35b: Reduce travel to a small weight shift or use a stable support if balance is uncertain.
messages.s_67342241292315ca709696e42ca0dbabb67d5b: Stop if you stumble, the floor slips, or pain changes your gait.
messages.s_e264258930cba023083e3330a80c3b61a5ed81: Original overhead foot map and wide side view; arrows show lead-then-rear and rear-then-lead, never crossing.
messages.s_3ab36fa3834dd7b37dac6f17b08004bb4beb56: Carry the stance to either side while keeping the same usable spacing.
messages.s_c9a47aa4117e88da3375f148988a3953467efa: To the lead side, lead foot starts; to the rear side, rear foot starts. The other foot follows rather than overtaking.
messages.s_b659b3ee813a6b14446acca9d5bff6f8fd433d: Keep the head within the base and the hands in guard. Do not drag the trailing foot across the floor.
messages.s_155d85092a346c4078898e43469dfc20757c76: Overtaking or joining the feet with the following foot changes the base in a side step. Let the foot nearer the direction start and the other restore spacing.
messages.s_9fe251e05392db2f3e46f32ae28917e71b11a2:
Take four small steps to each side and reset after each pair; reverse your lead side and repeat once.

Short focused practice: Stop fully after the first two steps each way, then mix the same paths in your chosen order in the second short section. Keep the guard comfortable. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Connect a side step after a forward-back pair while keeping the base.
