messages.s_2d4a314dbfcfddd4b7216cd210448b036e4b8b: For this paused learning drill, keep the exit separate: count “hands home, then feet”. This is a way to practise the parts in order, not a rule that all boxing footwork must wait for both hands.
messages.s_2e7dc62777b4aa61e88313ca685408df6a54c4: For one small lateral pair, select the foot on the movement side first; the follower restores spacing. Do not cross the feet. Plan the return while stopped; use a paper diagram without travel if balance is uncertain.
messages.s_2ec5df7fc51f32264d0ed2fcc10edf348dbe95: Begin in comfortable short front preparation without adding a step. messages.s_3482c5f96a59902fea12677704233fcb061bb0: This orientation task is not a traditional kata pivot. First rest the hands at the sides; use lesson 8’s rear-foot-to-level exit from the short front position to parallel neutral and stop. This proposal’s walking right quarter-turn has four foot placements: right → left → right → left. Initial forward is N; the target on your own right is E. (1) Lift the right foot and place it a small amount forward-right, comfortably pointing toward the intermediate direction between N and E. (2) Lift and advance the left a small amount, keeping it on a separate track to the left of the right, pointing toward the same intermediate direction. (3) Lift the right and place it farther along the short curved path, comfortably toward E. (4) Lift the left and place it level on the left side of the right, parallel and comfortably toward E. Keep each placement separate and small; settle quietly at each placement and stop completely once both feet are settled at the end. The foot changing direction lifts first; do not drag/twist the other loaded sole or force it around with the torso. No crossing, jump or turning strike. No personal P3/P6 validation of these selected step angles/lengths or support suitability is supplied; do not force the written diagram into four physical steps. Use the separate small walking adaptation or stay with written study. After stopping at E, separate right-forward preparation starts by moving the right foot a small amount forward on its own track. When the separate exit needs a walking left quarter-turn, mirror it as left → right → left → right: first two placements toward the intermediate leftward direction, last two toward the target; the final right foot comes level on the right side of the left. A walking half-turn is two same-direction quarter sequences, not a planted pivot. The fixed foot orders in this paragraph are original written heading preparations, with no demonstration or physical acceptance supplied. The separate non-contact task teaches an ordinary small walking adaptation; do not count them as the same physical performance.
messages.s_353a34dc756e78a654f9b563c892e8678efc24:
Imagine a small X on the floor. Take one comfortable small diagonal step along a ray, let the other foot restore your base, then return to the centre before choosing another ray. No arm-length distance is required.

Short focused practice: Try the two front rays of a small X first, then the two back rays after a rest. Stop at the centre on every return and name the next direction beforehand. Rest between sections; take longer if you need it.

When comfortable, try changing just one variable: Choose the small X rays in a different order while keeping the return to the centre.

Next practice: At the next suitable session, recall the short sequence without reading first. Briefly revisit Forward and back; check only the confusing part again.

messages.s_47afd4610b761683abe0fc27ca13c2c0897f3d: KA-P1 Two lines has six original practice units. A is the starting area, B the first left-forward settlement, C the area after the right foot passes forward, and D the area after the left passes forward toward E. These are body areas, not single-foot targets; both feet retain separate tracks. C needs clearance for the rear foot coming level, the four-placement walking right turn and separate right-forward preparation; D also needs space for neutral finishing and the walking turn after the sequence. The separate return route is D→C west W, C→A south S, ending at A facing N; these are paper labels relative to initial N/E, not a required compass. Lesson 15 supplies the exit’s foot order. This proposal’s paper return template uses two forward right-left placements on each straight segment and a closing right foot brought level with the left; draw these small footprints within the areas’ clearance in advance without crossing. This written diagram does not validate personal step lengths or clearance; do not compress the path into an inadequate room. If the selected foot order does not fit, do not invent extra steps for an exit; retain a written task and open adaptation question. Do not mirror the written KA-P1 plan. In the optional physical task, explore only the clear space separately with ordinary small walking steps; this does not accept the fixed KA-P1 foot order.
messages.s_47f947e94f8e234fd6757fe69e1f07071cb25c: While seated, try one small forward–return hand path and rest, then work the other hand separately. If comfortable, try a small forward–return sequence with both palms without pressing them together, then lower them; use no partner push or power target. This original arm sequence recalls one right entry with multiple arm phases, without validating traditional sub-techniques.
messages.s_4aaa59eecabf62558f05ea9592e400e618edbd: For a small lateral pair, the movement-side foot starts and the follower restores spacing. Face the same direction. Add no crossing, circling or turning direction change; you may explain it on paper without travel.
messages.s_4cd7a78aaecb0cf030498f0d017404ba49ea9c: Lead-hand path→same guard→pause; then a clear comfortable small rear-hand path→guard→pause. Explain the second path on paper if the preceding turn is uncertain. This is not a fast one-two, strike power or combat timing.
messages.s_4f5c141e7585ead4246dd8315c21c8046689ab: This original curriculum has no acceptance of instructor review, JabLab demonstration or individual feedback. These records do not make separately published small non-contact self-practice instructions personally physically validated, and do not create mandatory outside approval in place of self-practice. Actual inspection of a reference video does not verify every hidden detail or every learner’s suitability. Audio must be inspected separately if audible emphasis is to be taught; no kiai or breathing key was inferred from muted viewing.
messages.s_4fc2266a106b7e2aca4b2e560ce364834a119b: Identify the returning hand’s own-side preparation; do not count it as pulling an opponent or successful defence.
messages.s_52932feaa0a5347d5018d3783e6def96982ec3: Count 3 is right hand/E; the next section starts from the preceding actual finish. A walking preparation does not validate the reference pivot.
messages.s_59f3b11f7532602b9bf990d803ae47c41a358b: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. messages.s_5de6b50eb9084a39d50982e5797b66d96be2c7: This lesson’s table is for H2 A. Try small left–centre and right–centre parts separately without sudden pushing; stop at each centre or finish the lesson. To study link C, use the separate preparation and table in lesson09. Do not continue pain, dizziness or unsafe balance for smoothness.
messages.s_61f9b73e2eb8eb618ab86062854233c0c4340d: Identify the advancing rear foot, its separate track and the absence of added hand technique.
messages.s_62233aaaca6a442b7f6fe9b0aae9b4c3ec00de: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. messages.s_68b5ca9c221e3f58c95d6109e81a04b7aaf070: From small left-front preparation, advance the right rear foot on its own track and stop completely. Then move the right hand from side preparation on a short straight path, keeping left hikite calm. Pause and return the right hand along the same path. Rest the hands and exit by aligning the rear foot beside the front. Work the other side separately. This beginner adaptation separates step and hand; do not try to accelerate them together.
messages.s_6981ca4297217fb49139556db75cdf792b821d: Seated, indicate your own left/right hand and name the lead hand and foot of the selected stance. Add no travel or stance switching.
messages.s_6b361ef9a9ecdafb6ff5ce6b62de0f606a604a: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Does completing the written sequence accept actual checks, clinch and Wai Kru?
messages.s_6d0a81c9f30f27bf5164c393caab456d7d9eee:
A 16-lesson pathway for an adult with no experience. The endpoint is preparing a suitable space, explaining lead/rear in a chosen stance, planning small steps and jab/cross returns, explaining the front kick's preparation–extension–retraction–landing order, and directing two short non-contact practice blocks from an original plan. Only the small, slow, non-contact options explicitly offered by the relevant lesson are optional in this first release. Seated, grounded or written work is also valid. The lesson counter is written self-review; it does not establish verified physical technique or individual suitability. This level does not complete the entire kickboxing domain, confer a belt, establish competition readiness or certify self-defense.

Kickboxing combines punching and kicking. WAKO defines distinct ring and tatami disciplines [S1]; this course does not deliver their competitive programs. “A” denotes JabLab's original solo beginner scope. Absence of contact does not establish that a movement suits an individual. No health, treatment, fall-prevention or performance outcome is promised.

Neither boxing nor Tai Chi completion is required. The learner must distinguish their own left/right, understand the instructions and act on a stop decision. Respect movement restrictions; obtain individual professional guidance if suitability is uncertain. This adult solo route does not automatically apply to children or people needing supervision.

Use a level, dry, nonslip floor, comfortable movement clothing, water nearby and a place to rest. Avoid slippery socks, loose rugs, jewelry and trailing cables. Suitable footwear or bare feet depend on the surface and instructor guidance; do not turn against a foot stuck to the floor. Keep people, animals, furniture and glass outside punching/kicking reach. No target, bag, gloves, wraps or weights are required; adding them does not authorize impact work. A stable fixed counter serves only as support; do not reach for or strike it. The phone is for reading; no camera or scoring is required.

Check the space before every physical lesson. If comfortable, walk slowly for 30–60 seconds or make small seated shoulder/hand movements, then use the easy stance task. These durations are suggested caps, not requirements. Begin with small range and slow speed. Do not hold or force the breath or attach it to counts; keep breathing comfortably. Pause and rest after a few attempts. Finish with comfortable walking or seated rest. Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unsafe balance or unusual discomfort; use safe support/rest and do not retry the harder task that session. Seek professional advice for continuing symptoms and urgent help for severe/sudden symptoms. This text gives no diagnosis or return-to-activity clearance. Stop after suspected head injury and seek individual health guidance [S8].
messages.s_6f1273c9dfaec531276b15757d25231d7a3797: Describe your own side names, the hand-part order and where you stopped. Say unknown for uncertain contact, foot loading or angles; an attempt is not proof of correct technique.
messages.s_71cdf33804d497b231f815fa5d20dc14a69fa9: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. messages.s_76d3e490c60c43425e0a131815451c873cd53d: Distinguish fist, kick, knee and elbow by name and learn the cultural headings. Describe this course’s selected beginner scope in your own words without imitating Wai Kru or combat technique.
messages.s_7963c59799faa37bffb0442ff07ec04ec2d5a3: Look ahead and to your own right first: keep people, objects, cables and slippery surfaces out of the hand and small-step paths. Rest your hands in an ordinary comfortable stance. Take just one ordinary small step and stop fully; another attempt is optional. If you need stable support, do not choose later hand/step tasks that require releasing it; draw the floor plan while seated.
messages.s_79b1fe08ef1faadd97992effbb769362c3b57c: While seated, bring the right hand slightly forward/up, at most to lower chest, while leaving the left near the thigh, then rest. If the sides become confusing, name them without movement first; do not force the shoulder overhead. This prepares recognition of right-higher/left-lower, not a front-heel lift or the form’s stance.
messages.s_7b0115d05f87ae42cbb5ff13ebe4e36b285b14: In a clear visible space, rehearse or try one small forward pair and, after pausing, one backward pair: lead starts forward, rear starts backward, follower preserves spacing. Add no bounce, punch or speed. Use paper arrows if space is uncertain.
messages.s_7b122ce44bfd97e1f5dfef55c21306fc6cf1cd: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Do gloves authorize bag strikes?
messages.s_7b24da1ed19f0992462fcf7c587f0caeb0f2a3: Pause between the short lead-hand path and its return. Show the rear-straight path separately only when the preceding small turn is comfortable and understood; otherwise keep the rear hand at guard. Do not turn them into a fast combination.
messages.s_7b48bf90fe0f8852b41a4f3ba38f54dc07c06c: The written counter counts written comparison only and keeps its existing per-visit meaning. A non-contact rehearsal self-report is not personal technique validation, mastery or rank; an unrecorded attempt is not presented as saved.
messages.s_7b61a3ea75953345166a687a2494bd30870a88: Choose just one earlier small hand task. Observe one question in one attempt: does the returning hand come to its own side? Then rest the hands. Leave unseen wrist or knee angles “unknown”. Try one specific change only in a later symptom-free rested attempt on the same short path; add no speed.
messages.s_7dc16302233751e98a6f2a44b9329515bf740b: Bring one hand comfortably beside the lower ribs with its elbow near the body. Keep the other hand’s forward travel small. Exchange the roles slowly once, then rest both hands. Do not yank the returning elbow backward, squeeze the shoulder back or swing the trunk. If a hand is needed for support, omit the two-hand task and describe one hand path while seated.
messages.s_7e03ee48c12d468b79017526c9c2d6d15133a9: Original JabLab beginner content: written recall and small non-contact self-practice. Source viewing scope is recorded separately; no personal technique, physical correctness or expert endorsement is claimed.
messages.s_80461f1f079b72e2e8305e347cadf35dd14308: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. messages.s_81a6405ec25d9fe514ed21914c83c842401ddf: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: What is the foot order when the left-leading example advances and returns to the same base?
messages.s_83dc684293c6879ba9aa4f59229f9cab64d455: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Does a planned backward step prove I can evade an opponent?
messages.s_8435c947eeef75293598ffbd93cff5d8014407: You may skip movement and explain your own left/right, hand order and stopping reason in words. Return to a smaller option in another comfortable session; physical retry in the same session is not required.
messages.s_8473ee493d920f41adc1308663b209b85dc34b: One small forward pair: lead starts and rear restores base spacing. After pausing, rear starts the backward pair. Each foot stays on its own track; add no punch, bounce or fast shuttling. Paper F/R arrows are a valid alternative.
messages.s_86d0e9697d9f8db82e06ccbce36916d699d582: Rest the hands comfortably beside the thighs and stop. If you practised standing, keep support and rest in your comfortable finishing position; finishing does not require bringing the feet together. No unseen right/left gathering step is taught; tried/skipped/uncertain reporting does not mean form mastery.
messages.s_89253919750d86e0d80e701e33e24ed361c2b3: Draw areas A–D on paper; they are body areas, not single-foot targets. Only if the actual path is clear, rest the hands and walk from the start to the end of the first short line in ordinary small steps, then stop. Do not compress the onward or return route into a small room or leave raised/loose floor markers. If both lines and the return do not fit, stay with the paper plan without adding the hand sequence.
messages.s_8a6221c57988f5341a3a4ad8bea6b6d491a7e5: With the rear elbow bent, show a very short horizontal path on its own side and return to guard; keep the other hand comfortably at guard. Start with a small arm path without turning the torso, or a paper diagram. Add no pivot without comfortable coordination; aim for no head contact, partner, spin or cutting effect.
messages.s_8aa7f92bafcf38e76e8e5f01d9ec32615f197a: 8→9 is long left and 9 is left/E. Cropping at 9 and occlusion at 12 remain unknown detail.
messages.s_8ab3dadfb3f377b8f71e0c5f7f208b563420d8: Optional small non-contact self-practice for adult beginners, without personal technique validation. Stance, hand-path and heading preparation do not establish a traditional kata performance.
messages.s_8c6e6c99f9799068ae2df2ad79fd3d0acf8390: A written-review report for this visit says you wrote your own answer, compared it with the key and recorded one correction or remaining question. Notes and the visit counter are not saved and may clear on a pause, course exit or account change. A prior written review is a prerequisite for the next written task. Unattempted, uncertain and attempted are distinct reports; none is observed technique, physical suitability, certification, a form score or mastery.
messages.s_8d80d807371cb9101b9d9a3f3bd619c9905cae: While seated, hold the left palm comfortably upright in front of the trunk, no higher than lower chest and without locking the elbow. Place a relaxed right fist below the left forearm at a comfortable distance from the body, then lower both hands without pressing on the forearm. No heel placement or single-leg loading task is assigned.
messages.s_9436b46f7c6e2772d5e83c51dbc94f490f1f93: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: In 5 load stays on left, toes point forward and left lands farther forward. In 6 load stays on right and right becomes lead; left starts backward. Is this the same arrangement? Write correct support, ball/toe arrangement, recovery base and hand closure/opening order.
messages.s_9476b3e62ac4ad0c5fca27dba7019b657fe08e: First examine a small heel–knee–hip–shoulder relation on two feet without extending the arms. Do not turn without a comfortable coordinated path; never force the torso over a stuck foot. A very short rear-hand path is a separate optional step; use only a two-foot guard or paper if uncomfortable.
messages.s_950c8c81fd69d7f4772348834ce0340219f013: Describe or try a very small weight shift with both feet on the floor; lifting a foot is not required. Do not reach for support that is not safely accessible. If uncertain, write seated which foot would support.
messages.s_978f121cb987fcf4417ea6b2e2683103414995: For this lesson select A’s right–centre half only, once: with both hands on fixed support and both soles down, use5–6 to move the body as a whole very slightly right without fully unloading the left leg. On7–8 return to your comfortable starting centre, stop and rest. Add no step, foot turn, waist side-bend or shoulder reach. Depth is not a goal; do not bend awkwardly to inspect knee direction, and record unknown if unobservable. Counts are not second or breath targets.
messages.s_9aa4bf6b418b923c7870379a416c72c373273c: Text and optional paper/pencil are enough. F0/R0 and F1/R1 are paper foot locations; no floor markers or objects to move around are required. For optional small movement, choose a level, dry, nonslip space clear of people and objects; keep the written option if the path is uncertain. Target no wall, bag, pad, animal or person. The phone is for reading, not a technique score or camera measurement.
messages.s_9c0388092cf5c14f35afbcb948fc81d0cabbd5: A small walking turn does not validate a traditional kata pivot or the physical KA-P1 pattern.
messages.s_9cec783168e67c333b6fc13242ac39969c80b2: With both feet in place, move the lead hand a very short distance forward and back to its own guard; keep the other hand comfortably in place. Bend neither wrist nor elbow to a hard stop; strike nothing. If a fist is uncomfortable, trace the path open-handed and record that it is not a strike.
messages.s_9d46488654f95e03077bf251c699391d7a7803: Areas A–D are not metres, camera measurements or a universal step length.
messages.s_9ed41c5afe430f88d131cfc959f7ca5fc562b7: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: In the left-leading example, does exit pull the left foot back or pass the right foot ahead of it?
messages.s_9fc72a5009a00e5af350623cfb099736777b23:
Check ordinary comfortable movement and clear non-slip space first. Do not test pain or uncertain balance by forcing a movement. Do not choose a task that requires releasing needed support; written study or seated hand/heading description remains an alternative.

End the attempt on pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, instability, a caught foot or a twisting sensation at the knee/foot. Rest the hands and stop using only ordinary comfortable movement. Do not test a symptom by retrying; obtain suitable health or movement support when needed.

One small part once is enough; repetition is optional. When symptom-free and rested, you may choose the same small part again. Do not increase speed, range and duration together; use no impact, partner, target, jump or breath holding.
messages.s_a0a20d13ce7ac2fd1b98429455b27f05ca01d6: Adult beginner scope only: small, slow and non-contact. Strike no target; add no partner, high kick, spin, jump or fall. Add no movement with a catching foot, discomfort, dizziness, instability or unclear direction; reach safe rest and do not retry the harder task that session.
messages.s_a32ea43eefc2d15455686f606b34897af59d9a: The selected starting and recovery position has both fists comfortably beside the lower ribs; each elbow stays near its own side of the torso and each palm points comfortably toward upward. In short left-forward position, bring the left fist across the front of the chest toward the right shoulder with a comfortably bent elbow; do not touch the face/throat. The right hand moves to a small soft forward preparation. Keeping near the torso, the left forearm follows a comfortable down-and-out path and stops in empty space above the left front thigh, without hitting the leg. Keep the elbow soft and the wrist in its straight relationship; this proposal brings the ending palm comfortably toward downward. The right fist returns to right lower-rib hikite. Pause. Then bend the left elbow comfortably at its own left side and move the left fist from the empty endpoint above the thigh on a short up-and-back path near the torso to the left lower ribs; comfortable forearm rotation brings its palm toward upward. The right stays quiet in right hikite. Both hands thus return to the defined start; the left does not circle in front of the face or via the right shoulder again. On the right-forward side, the right prepares near the left shoulder and descends above the right thigh; the left returns to left hikite. After the pause, the right fist follows the same short up-and-back path at its own right side to the right lower ribs while left hikite stays. Before the next oi-zuki, both fists wait in these side preparations; only the hand on the new forward side extends after the foot settles. This explicit recovery, small static path and palm/endpoint choice are original adaptations with no P2/P5 personal physical validation; no incoming-strike interception is claimed. Optional small non-contact practice is shown separately from those validations.
messages.s_a7b4161734da91700747da38ecd7a636c78458: With the hands resting, study the path from 16 into 17 by continuing left from S through E, N and W in small ordinary steps, then stop facing W. A short right turn is a different path; stay on paper if space is insufficient. Rehearse the separate parts: left downward path/W at 17, right hand/W at 18, right downward path/E after the right half-turn at 19, and left hand/E at 20. Stop completely at 20; add no 21st punch or boxing guard.
messages.s_a90b1b52c3351665587dbc6fe931abe6838e84: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: If the right hand returns but heel/hip remain in the extended position, is recovery complete?
messages.s_aa47b44713b09be5f12abab9dbfcfb9d54f3fb: With the source hidden, recall the selected side, backward step order, guard return and A–D. Record your own attempt as unattempted/uncertain/attempted; after one correction, recheck the same small task or written alternative. Claim no physical correctness, mastery or instructor approval.
messages.s_aa9195f25b89416501a9ea79036c9f45f80099: Recall the written foot–hand match from the same start first. In optional small non-contact practice, you may choose just one part again when symptom-free and rested. Do not test it again after pain, binding or uncertain balance in the previous attempt. This retry does not accept any P record or validate technique.
messages.s_aaa70854df2a484ac76e9beed684d7362b55ab: Keep the feet still. Move one hand from side preparation along a short slow straight path into empty space, leaving the elbow soft rather than driving it to the end. The other hand returns calmly to hikite. Pause, return along the same short path and rest. Try the other side separately after resting. Use no target, impact, full speed, sharp hip twist or breath holding.
messages.s_af6d754456ddc3c916f720f6cfd711ddedaf40: With the text hidden, explain one foot order and two different recoveries; write one uncertainty and correction. Later recall the same small task or written alternative again. Keep unattempted, uncertain and attempted separate; infer no completion of Muay Thai, defense or physical mastery.
messages.s_b08e4e318a3013186d5a7a07804cb846199262: Distinguish a clear actual path from a paper plan, and identify space in which to stop.
messages.s_b118137f43430197d26fcf9e16d23e577d1059: The order is left/N at 5, then right–left–right; no extra ready position is counted at the boundary.
messages.s_b12d4e747d26919eb6ac650ac65d530692e7a3: The right hand works when the right foot is forward, and starts after settling.
messages.s_b33a1c5f912185ba66f3a2482ed9c80b6d5a33: Read the explanation first, close it and write your own answer. Consult the key afterward. Record one concrete correction or open uncertainty and plan a suitable written retest. The optional small non-contact task is shown separately; it does not accept P records, validate personal technique or award written progress. Recheck space and stop conditions after a break; an earlier answer or comfort is not automatic continuation.
messages.s_b4a5706294c40b62fd3b1994e731e5e34d3a2a: Separate attempted, unattempted and uncertain parts. Explain direction and return in your own words; award no correctness grade to unobserved or unmeasured technique.
messages.s_b6335afcc60456ac4485103cd6a4c7b63b73d3: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Does tucking the thumb into the palm first and closing the other fingers over it match this fist example? Write the closure/opening order. Can source majority alone accept a guard with a different palm direction?
messages.s_b72c3ea2bb786211a04fda9014d88cc4c283ad: Keep A’s opening separate from B’s already-ready start; infer no unseen pressure or heard kiai.
messages.s_b7ce2e8fb44cb766a4a173a0b33c9800f77170: Distinguish the meanings of check and clinch; attempt no partner work, real strike or single-leg defensive response. Do not present opponent timing from a source as solo competence. Write on paper why these need separate instruction.
messages.s_b7d49a9c9638836995c286eb804881e7c05de4: Explore the left turn and right half-turn separately with the hands resting and small walking steps; do not force the trunk around one planted foot. Then rehearse 1–2 in a small range: left turn/left downward path, then right-front/right short straight hand in the same W heading. Stop fully. Rehearse the right turn from 2 into 3 separately; the right arm folds near the opposite shoulder before the right downward path facing E. Count 4 is left-front/left short straight hand toward E. Pause between parts and add no boxing guard.
messages.s_b9616697d98f2e437ae6f63985b235200ba5dc: The sixth unit ends with a stop; returning is not a seventh technique. Uncertain order or a stop condition does not complete a full sequence.
messages.s_bc0e0c9b4767ca12cac0c35ebc758164479d4f: Keep the feet separate at a comfortable width and avoid locking the knees. Rest the hands without tightening the shoulders. Settle briefly, then return to an ordinary comfortable stance. Do not force parallel feet, deepen the stance or set a long holding target.
messages.s_bc61c2adfd44c232d1a5f0cdbf2626a2c30dba: First explain the teep order verbally or with the hands on two feet: prepare→brief extend→re-bend→return to the original base. The optional low, small, non-contact trial is an original JabLab beginner adaptation, not a copy of the partnered source demonstration. Keep both feet grounded unless preparation is comfortable and steady. Add no target, hip drive, arm swing, backward lean or height. Return the foot slowly to its starting track without crossing; use the grounded sequence without leg extension if foot position or balance is uncertain.
messages.s_bf0d382805891bf58ccae74fde71904830b8c0: For written work, record the uncertain part in your own answer; you may stop or take a break, and must not invent progress. During optional small movement, add no movement and reach safe rest with discomfort, dizziness, instability, a catching foot or unclear direction; do not retry the harder task that session. Do not practise abrupt freezing on a raised leg or during a turn, hopping or a forced pivot. Seek appropriate health support for continuing symptoms and urgent help for severe or sudden symptoms. This text gives no diagnosis or personal movement clearance.
messages.s_c0a45c2720d1dffb03aa7eb853d8e87e2a6f07: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: If weight remains on right while the right rear knee lifts, the lower leg extends like a kick and right lands ahead of left, does that describe this preparation’s start/return? Write the correct transfer and rear return.
messages.s_c2d70767f9a25ec206e922c6b575647569f760: Preserve left/W at 17 and left/E at 20; arm/foot overlap at 16→17 does not prove loading or a pivot edge.
messages.s_c3749a6c7673367efa4740df4a6a6c81827c9a: First describe a small body turn and return without extending the arms into a strike. Do not turn if foot, knee and hip do not move comfortably together; never force the torso against a stuck foot. A stationary two-foot guard or paper explanation is the beginner alternative.
messages.s_c3b76f00acaf66dccf478f20fbd6b6b2740686: Sit comfortably or stand. Gently curl four fingers from an open hand, keeping the thumb outside. Do not shape the fist by bending the wrist. Reopen and rest the hand. Try one hand first; after a rest, the other is optional. Do not strike a surface, seek a maximum squeeze or bear weight on the fist.
messages.s_c8b7716ef576882e6ef92270ab8837c78d1b05: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: In a left-leading stance does the left lead always start a move right?
messages.s_c8f45084dd76d275cda19cf9b1fe4c8ad20c9f: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Does correctly answering the MT-P1 key prove defense/check or clinch skill?
messages.s_cad8d200bd4778309190b3d2cd6657c0337d12: Stop the practice immediately if symptoms, pain or loss of balance appear. Rest instead of continuing with a changed plan. Do not resume while the symptom remains; seek appropriate health advice if it persists, returns or concerns you.
messages.s_cc74eecf518c09d7877cb607df0e31bfb77617: In this paused drill, both hands were back before my exit began.
messages.s_ccc8fa6ad339b00e89f232658222dd05779975: Recall the opening, 1–4, 5–8, 9–12, 13–16, 17–20 and closing aloud first. You may rehearse each section separately as a small non-contact attempt, with rests or stops between sections. Choose to link the whole order slowly only when the entire path is clear and the earlier parts do not require forcing. If a count or heading is lost, stop and return to the text rather than catching up at speed. Added pauses and step–hand separation are beginner adaptations, not a standard kata performance or physical pass.
messages.s_ccd6e039a0bc017ac5297cee9e0daeeae8f9cc: The lesson’s existing written progress meaning stays unchanged; this creates no physical acceptance or video review evidence.
messages.s_cd18f18334a725efd88159d07639c62edbaa85: Paper and a pen are enough for written work. For optional small non-contact practice, check a clean, level, nonslip space without obstacles or other people and see the foot, hand and exit paths in advance. Use no loose rug, slippery socks or raised floor marker. If support is needed, do not select a task that requires releasing it; use seated written study or one-hand description instead. Use no bag, makiwara, partner or striking target.
messages.s_cee81a6618325372094320f52b0e66aa3279d9: Recall the reference opening from the text first: bow, upright, left outward, right outward with crossed arms, ready. If you choose to rehearse it, check the space, keep a comfortable foot width and use small unforced movements. Joining the heels or making a deep bow is not required; label any change a “beginner adaptation”. If balance or comfort is uncertain, recall the order on paper only. Do not add an opening bow to recording B.
messages.s_d01b198ed3166ad3feecce3e2db982373cb1a8: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Did the knee/torso turn without the rear foot, and did the lead hand remain in guard?
messages.s_d02768b4833368a8441286c5204cd879bb781f: While seated, open the hands through a small comfortable path and lower them toward the thighs; you may work one hand before the other. Rest with natural breathing. Distinguish official 16 Closing from separate Return to Normal; add no new step or forced foot gathering.
messages.s_d0abeb3846b1dd19d20a71b0b8375382370d08: This is shortened preparation for zenkutsu-dachi, not acceptance of the full standard stance. From the parallel start, move the left foot a comfortable small amount forward on its own left track; the right remains behind on a separate right track. The front knee retains its relationship with the foot direction; do not collapse inward or twist the knee/torso over a planted sole. Keep the rear knee soft, heel/sole relationship comfortable and torso quiet. There is no universal angle, knee depth or load percentage; the personal position is not validated by this course. This proposal selects the following neutral exit: first rest the hands at the sides and stop; keep the left front foot in place, lift the right rear foot and take a small forward step on its own right track until level with the left, without passing it. Both feet settle parallel at a comfortable width; stop completely. From right-forward, reverse this: right front foot stays, left rear foot advances on its own left track until level with it. No feet-together position, crossing, jump or rotation of a loaded sole. The exit also uses space ahead; if space or comfort is missing, do not attempt this diagram physically. This explicit foot order is an original short-preparation adaptation; no P3 personal physical validation is supplied. The optional small task and stop/alternative instructions are shown separately.
messages.s_d26a89c7b5bb0b20c2caa85749acb58ea0cab6: Describe only what you can see about the outside thumb and unforced wrist; keep the hand open if closing it is uncomfortable.
messages.s_d2b00ca90f10a3cb01008ccd91e17fd9dc6fbd:
You may use the existing written task or recall question without choosing a physical attempt. Written answers, correction and retest stay separate.

This small, paused, non-contact beginner adaptation does not validate personal technique, health, rank or traditional kata performance. Do not count the exact written order and an ordinary walking adaptation as the same performance. No physical attempt awards written progress.
messages.s_d2e30b65c6d3dbdec10abe8b0e3d8bdcbe2304: Unit four starts right-forward at C: first rest both hands at the sides; keep the right front foot in place and bring the left rear foot forward on its own left track until level with the right; stop in parallel neutral. Use lesson 12’s right-left-right-left walking turn from N to E and stop once both feet settle. Move the right foot a small amount forward toward E on its own right track, settle separately right-forward and stop. Bring both fists beside the lower ribs; right gedan-barai preparation and left hikite, then pause. From the empty endpoint above the right thigh, return the right fist on the short up-and-back path at its own right side to the right lower ribs; left hikite stays and both palms point comfortably toward upward. Unit five: the left rear foot passes forward toward E on its own left track; settle completely left-forward at D and stop. The left travels from left-side preparation on the short straight path while right hikite stays. After a pause, the left returns along the same short path to the left lower ribs. Unit six: rest both hands at the sides; the left front foot stays while the right rear foot advances on its own right track and stops level with the left. Both feet settle parallel, facing E, with a complete pause. KA-P1 ends here. The separate ordinary walking exit is: at D, take the right quarter-turn twice (each right-left-right-left), facing E→S→W, then stop. Toward W, take a small right forward placement, a small left forward placement, then close by bringing the right level on the right side of the left into the C turning area, and stop. At C, use the walking left quarter-turn left-right-left-right from W→S and stop. Toward S, take a small right forward placement, a small left forward placement, then close with the right level beside the left into area A and stop. At A, take two walking right quarters S→W→N, each right-left-right-left, ending parallel neutral with a complete pause. On each straight segment the final right foot does not pass the left. Draw areas/footprints for this selected order in lesson 13 beforehand; walk while seeing the space, with no blind backward step, invented extra step or twisting a loaded sole. If the diagram does not fit personal space/comfort, do not attempt the physical exit; retain a written task and open adaptation question. The separate exit is not a kata technique or seventh unit; no P3/P6 personal physical validation of the complete fixed diagram is supplied. In the separate small non-contact task, you may set up the second line independently and leave by ordinary walking while seeing the path; that adaptation is not the same performance as the written fixed foot order.
messages.s_d405e49410895b273573e2d03e8aeb0e0e4d99: While seated, hold the left palm forward a small comfortable distance and place the right hand below and slightly inward from the left forearm. Keep the elbows soft, rest both hands, and name which hand is forward. Heel placement and gathering the rear foot are not part of this preparation.
messages.s_d54e2aad8f3806b46e3194283b6d03ee42cb3f: Order the nine MT-P1 pauses on paper first. If desired, show only the grounded stance–small step–short hand path–guard–backward step section with pauses; verbal teep, knee and elbow explanations are fully valid alternatives. Do not aim to finish the whole sequence fluidly or quickly; add no partner, target, spin or fall.
messages.s_d77ca99e1762028baa76b0aa5547caca860127: From a comfortable two-foot base, show a short lead-hand path and same-path guard return separately. Keep the other hand at its own guard. Add no wrist bend, hard elbow stop, step or target. You may choose an open-handed path explanation.
messages.s_d9efd591938fd440016c8eac1ba83429caa045: Choose one small component or written recall of the six units. Distinguish “written”, “small non-contact attempt”, “stopped” and “not attempted”; record one observation and the open question. These choices do not establish personal technique validation, rank or Heian Shodan achievement. You need not add speed or depth next time.
messages.s_dc0273cbdcc36e7975626a5f7ec6233714368d: The downward path, pause and own-side recovery are separate stages; add no hard pull or hip thrust.
messages.s_e0815296666520a11bdcf9eed9fd045e75f431: From a comfortable two-foot start, place one foot a very small distance back on its own track; face the same way and pause. Return the rear foot on its track only to lead-foot level. Require no fixed angle, deep stance, crossing or switch; draw it seated if needed.
messages.s_e35f282a0b9210a5fe308c336d32ed476cfe7b: Separate the left quarter heading change from count 12’s left hand/W finish with small walking steps and stop facing S. Rehearse left downward path/S at 13, followed by right–left–right small steps and same-side hands toward S at 14–16. Settle after each step and keep the hand paths small. Stop at right hand/S at 16 and name the next turn without erasing that finish. Add no detail to an obscured guide hand or wrist.
messages.s_e405358f494308e4ad9a2df046d77f1676996d: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Did I omit a return?
messages.s_e4630540059e43adf006ff39b78342271cb5b2: Choose one comfortable A cycle or half-cycle with H2; you may stop at each centre.
messages.s_e50faee2df132f3174bdfbc8eced0b2e88ed6c: This beginner course has a limited endpoint: explain scope and stopping; learn comfortable small parallel/front preparation, seiken/hikite, short choku-zuki, step–settle–same-side hand, a small gedan-barai path and walking heading changes; and compare the original six-unit KA-P1 order in writing. Optional non-contact self-practice instructions are shown separately. They do not establish personal technique or traditional kata performance acceptance.
messages.s_e578723dc878a6dc85ef81da598805bbf7e905: Check support and clear space first; name your own left and right without moving. If comfortable, choose a start with the feet already comfortably apart; do not try an opening step unseen in the video. Rest the hands comfortably beside the thighs and breathe naturally.
messages.s_e5e96e04bc79d4f17a2b28b9bf73733ffb5d92: Record what was observed, what was unseen and the single change separately.
messages.s_e9ad2c0900fda42acae6424ef664a0793cfaab: With both feet grounded, describe a small shift toward the rear foot and return to both feet. Lifting the lead foot is not required. A low bent knee is optional only when comfortable and steady; set no single-leg hold target. Explain without lifting if uncertain.
messages.s_e9b5c455f12b0dcf4f63f4663ec0549a2946ab: Completing KA-P1 does not establish a traditional kata, rank or defensive competence.
messages.s_e9d1ac4b6294b93dffd1c20cf08b8b06bfa288:
This first release is a selected 16-lesson beginner path. Writing your own answer, comparing with the source and making one correction are learning steps; they are not a technique score or mastery certificate. Physical correctness, individual suitability, instructor approval and independent learner outcomes are not presented as verified.

Optional small non-contact trials stay within each lesson’s explicit limits; add no forced turn, high kick, target impact, partner, spin or jump. A seated or grounded written option is always valid. This course names movement direction and recovery order explicitly instead of repeating the inconsistent S5 heading. There is no camera measurement or speed/force result.
messages.s_ea71ec29722f2ad3a22ca3401386b2693b64da: The floor path extends beyond the hand path. Plan clear space for the start, two short forward settlements, a rightward heading change and ordinary walking return. A paper plan is not an actual space check: look ahead and sideways for objects, people, cables and slippery patches. Do not choose a task that requires releasing needed support; if uncertain, stay with written study or seated description. Needing help is not a negative score.
messages.s_eea6fcee8dc3a4ba5031e9f3620ad16161ed47: Rest the hands and settle both feet in a comfortable neutral position first. Look to your own right and check the clear path. Lift the feet alternately in small ordinary walking steps to face right, settling at each placement and stopping at the end. Do not twist the trunk over a planted foot, jump or cross the feet. The written KA-P1 right-left-right-left pattern is a selected example; do not force your physical walking turn into four steps. If space or comfort is insufficient, show N→E on paper.
messages.s_f0de7e5916f93e937439d31b1315c1492b1336: Stop at the current unit when the order is lost; do not catch up by jumping, turning or adding speed.
messages.s_f1659237156d2d455fd53fbe51130a0b95666a: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Which leg supported, and could I return to the prior footprint?
messages.s_f1c57db32c94f6efd99fc40be7d983d072efd2: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: If the reader cannot explain teep recovery, should they repeat faster, and what should they record?
messages.s_f26b7ac0c5b6bd4bdc44f09588407dd4be3fb9: You may explain the order seated or with both feet grounded without performing the movement. Return to this lesson’s written question in your own words: Does low front-kick work complete roundhouse?
messages.s_f50b9a1d85be05b16afa00452ab7b2ee9c80b0: Any hand rotation is comfortable forearm movement, not a task to bend the wrist or lock the elbow.
messages.s_f8db47e1afabba40bef62185831ffaa983dded: Keep it slow, small and non-contact. Stop for pain, dizziness or unsafe balance; do not try standing work without support within reach. Do not turn a loaded planted foot, twist the knee or hold your breath; copy no uncertain backward step or half-turn.
messages.s_f906b10b855db84cbd5e550deb10990e0946ce: Show a relaxed guard, a pause and a check of clear space. A backward pair is optional and is added only with a visible clear return path. This planned rehearsal is not defense against an incoming strike or a reflex result.
messages.s_fa0830b9abd21074ade87df91f12c6c137eff2: TS-P0–TS-P5 track personal physical validation of space, stance, turns, hand paths and stopping; those validation records are not accepted. The separate optional small non-contact task does not accept them or validate personal suitability. Do not force an uncomfortable turn; use written headings or a floor plan when uncertain. Do not record earlier parallel preparation as replacing A’s toes-out ready position.
messages.s_fa1e8a26b54899a7bee78216f98a9f932f04c0: Visually check the space; name two obstacles and a resting place without adding standing movement. Seated review is an equivalent written option.
messages.s_fe693a0410fa4789f801cc7b33dc0029e2de7f: Open a comfortable hand, loosely curl four fingers and leave the thumb outside; keep the wrist aligned. Bring hands to their own guard without blocking vision and return to rest. Add no squeezing, impact or wrist bend; if uncomfortable, trace only the path open-handed.
messages.s_947bc56b68aad5653a47935fa1e700cdc67a32: Automatic assessment is not supported for this lesson.
messages.s_13e733b124e346b70b6e7792345f5976c43878: Not in this course: sparring, partner or bag work, and a built-in round timer. Time rounds with your own clock and finish with a few minutes of easy walking and breathing.
messages.s_55a263c59e9bb6bdf66300f01a7341c13d4182: Not in this course: roundhouse and side kicks, kick defence, blocking drills and timed rounds. The kick itself needs individual demonstration and feedback, which this app cannot give.
messages.s_b85442d4b944f432452e01bf1f5b2f32a90ee1: Not in this course: roundhouse kicks, blocks and checks, clinch practice, pivots and angles, and timed rounds.
messages.s_1d222ec6828e6dbc59996b3c7e3632a9ac5e6d: This course is the first layer of kihon. Not in it: mae-geri, age-uke, soto-uke, uchi-uke, gyaku-zuki, kiba-dachi and kokutsu-dachi.
messages.s_0bc0c5bcb95a5d5bf11953bca452db82799420: This course covers only the beginner kata Taikyoku Shodan; other kata and partner applications are not in it.
messages.s_c130ab10777d493083e8332dfcde980b566872: Not in this course: stepping, turning and the moving Yang Family 16 form. The written Yang 16 course describes the sequence; it does not teach its steps.
messages.s_62240753f49c343c019c7e487cd297e7bd128f: Before practice, walk slowly for a short time; finish with easy walking or seated rest.
messages.s_49ca58133a086acc186838629d10cb996fbe3f: Show preparation and return to the same footprint with both feet grounded. Keep both feet down: lifting a foot or the knee needs the individual demonstration and feedback this app cannot give. Add no hop, high knee or backward lean. If balance is uncertain, explain the order seated.
messages.s_18f6b66cf807489aacbd0a486448617410f4eb: Plan lead-hand path→guard→two-foot pause and the kicking order as separate blocks; explain the kick part with both feet grounded instead of kicking. Add no simultaneous punch and kick, reaching for support or speed.
messages.s_b45b33aae8ada6255395a9481caf4d6663391e: Explain A–D on paper or with the hands: prepare, briefly extend, re-bend, return to the original base. Keep both feet grounded; the kick itself needs the individual demonstration and feedback this app cannot give. Add no target, high kick or abrupt extension.
messages.s_5c41b8a10ca5a907c56a46957e982522df1262: While seated, move the left hand through a small comfortable arc above the left knee region toward the thigh without pressing on the knee. Separately move the right palm a short distance forward and lower it. No forward step or loading over the left knee is assigned. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_c4822bf09f9c8bf3e20e36cd126df5155ff60d: While seated, make a small comfortable circle with the left hand and lower it to the thigh, then try the right separately. Try one hand higher and the other lower only in a comfortable space between thigh and lower chest. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_246e405cb412bdd0ad993ea6607bb98dfbac67: While seated, loosely close both hands if comfortable; hold the left a little higher than the right, no higher than lower chest, then lower both. Recognize the hand order without forcing wrists/shoulders, contact, power or head-level striking. Name the new direction only; the approximate 90° interpretation is not a required body angle. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_e808981698354c8a7c1e819445a6cabdcff7f0: While seated, bring the right hand slightly forward/up while resting the left beside the hip/thigh, then lower the right. This prepares recall of the single right-sided appearance; do not count the next movement as a second Mane. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_9e5cf849968dcd911b697343829590bee2b3e3: While seated, hold one hand at a comfortable height around lower chest and the other near the thigh, then lower them separately and exchange positions. No head turn or overhead shoulder lift is required. This preparation does not teach E11’s approximate half-turn; name the new direction only. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_3f683ccb07e4d2c931a4e6efe53ca238b0ec93: While seated, move the left palm forward a small comfortable distance and rest it. Then separately extend and return a relaxed right fist along a small forward path without pressing the forearm or pushing the fist with the left palm. The unseen crossing or landing sequence is not taught here. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_8f626685bba87948522bc64433306d781e79a2: While seated, gather the right fingers loosely without forcing them and do not bend the wrist downward. Move the left open palm forward a small comfortable distance and lower it; the right hand need not match an exact hook. Name the new direction only; do not pivot or turn. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_0a4aa432f873734169163c36f411d91ce3b086: While seated, lower the left hand through a small path to the thigh. Extend and return a relaxed right fist along a small comfortable forward/downward path without locking the elbow or striking a target. The traditional target name assigns no contact with a person, and no forward step or power delivery is assigned. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
messages.s_0c4df7d7912f10675f80c4d4e04ea2c937772e: While seated, comfortably bring both forearms in front of the trunk; briefly make a crossed appearance without forcing the wrists, or describe the sequence only. Lower the hands separately and rest, with no hold-duration target. Name the new direction only; do not cross the feet or turn. Separate optional standing preparation: with support within reach, keep both feet where they are and make only a small comfortable weight shift. Stepping, foot placement and turning are not taught in this app.
